The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Outlawing zero-hours contracts could impose an annual cost on businesses of up to £3 billion, according to new Government analysis.

However, the proposed workplace reforms are nevertheless expected to "support growth" through the improvement of conditions for staff, an impact assessment published on Wednesday states.

The total direct expense to employers resulting from the ban is estimated to lie between £350 million and £2.9 billion each year, with figures showing an "indicative central" baseline of £1.1 billion.

Ministers are consulting on whether to extend the measures to anyone working 48 hours a week, though official preference remains a threshold between eight and 20 hours.

Ministers are consulting on whether to extend the measures to anyone working 48 hours a week ( Getty/iStock )

Ministers have defended the reforms by arguing they will help millions of workers who face uncertainty over their weekly hours and earnings, and unions have said a ban will help offer greater security in the event of shifts being cancelled at the last minute.

In its analysis, the Government said the proposals would mean workers were expected to receive payments of between £5 million and £1.2 billion because of the right to payments for shifts getting cut or moved at short notice.

It said the measures are expected to “support growth through improved worker wellbeing and engagement”, which research suggests is linked to increased productivity.

“There may also be wider benefits due to higher wellbeing and labour market participation. Stress, depression and anxiety accounted for 22.1 million lost working days in 2024/25, equivalent to around £6.5 billion in lost output,” the paper added.

But retailers said the potential costs outlined on Wednesday risk “a hammer blow to young people’s job prospects”.

Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the British Retail Consortium, said: “The scale of these costs raises serious questions about whether the guaranteed hours reforms will actually deliver value for workers, with the cost to employers appearing hugely disproportionate to the benefits for employees.

“These estimates also only tell part of the story, as retailers will have to fork out hundreds of millions of pounds to update their HR and payroll systems.”

She said the costs “could not come at a worse time” after the rise in employer’s national insurance contributions.

“Adding further costs when youth unemployment is soaring risks being a hammer blow to young people’s job prospects, at precisely the time businesses across the country need to be creating more opportunities,” she said.

The British Chambers of Commerce also voiced concern about the analysis and criticised the timing of its publication “so late in the consultation process”.

Kate Shoesmith, director of policy at the BCC, said: “The increased cost to businesses of the proposed changes to zero hours contracts will be a further hammer blow for many firms struggling to keep their heads above water.

“The Government had previously claimed that the cost of the entire Employment Rights Act for business would be £1 billion but this research clearly blows that out of the water.”

She added: “We are already facing a youth unemployment crisis – now is not the time to make it even more costly for employers to hire.

Kate Nicholls, chairwoman of UKHospitality, said: “The Government should be incentivising employment in hospitality, as a sector that employs the most young people, most part-time workers and the most non-graduates.

“Instead, these reforms add yet more cost, at a scale that far outweighs the cost benefits for employees.

“It’s critical the Government works with sectors like hospitality to reduce the cost of employing people and incentivise employment, rather than increasing costs and risking further lost job opportunities.”

Neil Carberry, chief executive of the Recruitment and Employment Confederation, voiced concerns that the assessment “undercounts the compliance and process costs businesses will face”.

“Rather than increasing job security, the proposals risk weakening a vital and successful part of the labour market that supports workforce participation, especially in sectors such as hospitality, retail and healthcare, and delivers economic growth,” he said.

“We are calling for more talks with Government to ensure that any final policy is coherent, proportionate and capable of operating effectively within the realities of the agency labour market.”

A Trades Union Congress spokeswoman said: “The Employment Rights Act will deliver an estimated £10 billion boost to the economy – that far outstrips any costs.

“Let’s stop the scaremongering. These are common sense reforms, which bring us closer to the European mainstream.”

A Government spokesperson said: “We are absolutely committed to ending exploitative zero hours contracts, where workers bear all the financial risk when hours, shifts and earnings are unpredictable.

“These reforms will give workers in every postcode greater income security and predictability of hours and while no final decisions have been made, we’re consulting to get the detail right and ensure this works in the real world.”

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Man Utd beat Leeds on penalties after selfie-seekers bring match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively but try explaining the half-hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only player the vast majority of crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta eyes Barcelona raid as £85m star opens door to transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta eyes Barcelona raid as £85m star opens door to transfer

Mikel Arteta is eager to improve his Arsenal squad ahead of the new Premier League season

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta continues plotting Arsenal's next move in the transfer market (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta remains focused on bolstering his Arsenal squad before the summer transfer window closes. The Premier League champions begin their title defence in eight days against Coventry City, but first face Manchester City on Sunday in the Community Shield.

‌



Despite missing out on Vinicius Junior after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid, the Gunners acquired his international team-mate Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United in a £75million deal.

‌



The 28-year-old's arrival marked Arsenal's fourth summer signing, but plans to add further remain among Arteta's priorities. The north London side are said to be targeting a Barcelona star, while an £85m-rated player has opened the door to an England move.

‌



Barcelona target emerges

Arsenal have attempted to sign defensive reinforcements this summer, but to no avail. William Saliba's absence for "an extended period" leaves Arteta without one of his best defenders ahead of the new season.

The Premier League champions have been interested in Aston Villa star Ezri Konsa but are set to turn their attention to Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, if the France international opens the door to a possible move, Spanish outlet Sport reports.

Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The outlet claims that Arsenal are looking for a centre-back, who can also cover the right side of defence. Kounde, 27, certainly fits the bill as prior to joining Barcelona, he played in central defence for Sevilla and moved to full-back after signing for the Catalan giants, which is a position he also plays for the national team.

Kounde is said to be a cheaper alternative to Konsa, who has been valued at £60million by the Europa League champions. The Frenchman has reported for pre-season training in Spain and played a key role in Barca's back-to-back title triumphs.

View 3 Images Jules Kounde is reportedly a target for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



£85m star open to Premier League move

Bayer Leverkusen star Christian Kofane revealed that he'd be open to joining the Premier League in the future. The 20-year-old impressed in his debut season with the Bundesliga club, with seven goals and nine assists in 44 games.

The striker came up against the Gunners last season in the Champions League round of 16 and showcased his potential in both legs despite his side coming up short. His agent Eric Depolo seemingly claimed that his performances led to the Gunners enquiring about his situation, but warned them that they'd have to part ways with £85m to get his client.

He told Daily Arsenal earlier this year: "Yes, Arsenal's interest is genuine. The manager [Mikel Arteta] likes him very much. I think it is too early to say [which club is leading the race].

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson backs himself to replace Rodri as he doubles down on Man Utd snub
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson backs himself to replace Rodri as he doubles down on Man Utd snub

Elliot Anderson talks about replacing Rodri, England's World Cup heartbreak and how his 10-year obsession with Manchester City made a move to United unthinkable

View 2 Images Elliot Anderson is ready to fill the boots of Rodri at Man City

Elliot Anderson admits he couldn’t care less about his price tag and is ready to be just as good as Rodri.

‌



Manchester City forked out a whopping £116million to Nottingham Forest - meaning the pressure for him to immediately succeed was immense.

‌



And that was before he was potentially given the job of filling the boots of Rodri, should City and Barcelona reach an agreement before the summer window closes. But rather than fearing the colossus challenge in front of him, Anderson believes he is up to the task.

‌



Anderson said: "It [the price tag] will always be (attached) to me. As long as I focus on myself and my performances, that’s all I can do. It's football, isn't it?

"Yeah, I think so (similar player to Rodri). I can be. I can do various things within midfield and I'll see where I get used. I'll play anywhere to be honest. Creating things, driving forward, or the other role, if they ask me to do that.

Kyle Walker lined up for immediate Premier League return after Burnley relegation READ MORE :

"I've spoken a few times to the manager. He explained the sort of things that I need to do. There is a lot of running, a lot of energy. It's to try and control games. That is what I can do."

‌



Anderson’s representatives opened talks with City before Pep Guardiola’s exit was announced, but he insists that made no difference to his decision.

When asked if it had an impact, he said: "Nope. Not at all. It's such a huge club and the players they have are the best.

"I think I knew of their interest shortly before the World Cup. I wanted to be surrounding myself with these sort of players, proving myself on a daily basis."

‌



Anderson wasted no time in winning the hearts of City fans, not only by snubbing Manchester United, but insisting that the city remains firmly blue. And he's now revealed a move to Old Trafford was never on the cards, thanks to a decade-long obsession with his new club.

View 2 Images Elliot Anderson is still not over England's heartbreaking exit at the World Cup (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

He said: "I've seen a few things (about what he said). It was blown out of proportion. I was probably eight or nine when (Sergio) Aguero scored that goal. I've been watching City for the past 10 years.

‌



"You've got a big decision to make - and I’m confident I've made the right one."

Anderson believes helping England reach a World Cup semi final proved he belongs on the biggest stage. But also one which has left him heartbroken, following the Three Lions' last-gasp defeat to Argentina in Atlanta.

‌



He added: "I take huge confidence knowing that I can perform on a World Cup stage. "Obviously I hadn't played in anything as big as that before. That was a really good test for me.

"It's really hard. I'm still sort of struggling with that now. There are highs and lows in football. It’s about how you bounce back. I’ve had three weeks to reflect on it, but now is a new season, you have to move forward."

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes' position decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly sends Arsenal message - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes' position decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly sends Arsenal message - 5 talking points

Arsenal took on Como at the Emirates Stadium in their final pre-season match before the Community Shield vs Man City

View 4 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid talk of him leaving Arsenal this summer

Arsenal have concluded their pre-season campaign, with eyes now on the weekend's Community Shield against Manchester City - the two teams meet in Cardiff on Sunday.

‌



In the final game before that meeting, the Gunners took on Italian side Como at the Emirates Stadium, a match which saw Cesc Fabregas return to his former home. The game ended in a 1-1 draw, with Arsenal winning thanks to a penalty shootout.

‌



Arsenal took the lead just after the first-half drinks break. Myles Lewis-Skelly capitalised on a mistake from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez. His clearance eventually found its way to Gabriel Martinelli, who got the ball back to the midfielder and he made no mistake to put Arsenal 1-0 up.

‌



But the Gunners didn't go into half time leading with Como making the most of a counter-attack. The ball made its way to Martin Baturina, who cut in from the left and gave Kepa Arrizabalaga no chance with a great finish to make it 1-1.

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That's how the score would remain, despite chances for both sides. That meant that penalties were needed to separate the two sides, with summer signing Christos Tzolis scoring the decisive spot kick.

‌



Mirror Football has taken a look at some of the biggest talking points from the game.

Myles Lewis-Skelly message

Like previous pre-season games, Lewis-Skelly was named in the starting XI, despite being linked with a move away from the Emirates in recent days.

The 19-year-old played in midfield just in front of the back four. He also got forward when given the chance, and was rewarded by scoring the opening goal.

‌



He capitalised on a mistake from the Como goalkeeper, to put Arsenal 1-0 up just after the first-half drinks break. His celebration saw him make a heart with his hands, which was a clear sign of where his head is at. He received a warm reception from the Emirates crowd when he was replaced in the second half.

Bruno Guimaraes role

Bruno Guimaraes completed a £75 million move to Arsenal from Newcastle United last week. The Brazilian came on at half-time to make his debut for the club, much to the delight of those at the Emirates. He played a similar role to Declan Rice, playing just in front of Lewis-Skelly.

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes made his Arsenal debut vs Como (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



As expected, Guimaraes was always eager to get on the ball and make something happen. He also got back well and helped prevent a counter-attack, leading to chants of 'Bruno' from the home crowd. His introduction did allow Lewis-Skelly to get forward a bit more often.

Defensive issues

Despite not giving up many chances in the first-half, Arteta would have been frustrated to concede one of the few that Como had. While it was a great finish, there may have been an argument that more could have done to stop the ball getting to that position in the first place.

Defensive concerns are something that has dominated pre-season, with the team having conceded three goals in each of their previous two games against Real Betis and Borussia Dortmund. It's something that Arsenal will want to tighten up going into Sunday's Community Shield.

‌



If Arsenal give Man City similar chances, then they are likely to take them. Even if the game is seen as a 'glorified friendly', losing to title rivals ahead of the start of the season is not the ideal preparation for their Premier League opener.

Mikel Arteta decision

Marli Salmon was again given a chance to impress for Arsenal as he was named alongside Gabriel Magalhaes at the heart of defence. The injury to William Saliba has left Arteta short in the area.

View 4 Images Cesc Fabregas was back at the Emirates

‌



They have been linked with Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, but it seems the two teams are still far apart in their valuation. Salmon could provide a solution if Arsenal are unable to bring in a new defender in the transfer window, having impressed again against Como.

Despite being just 16, he earned praise for his composure, strength and willingness to step out of defence with the ball when needed.

Either way, a decision will have to be made over his short-term future. But it will be a bit of a waiting game for Arsenal.

‌



Players have to be on a professional contract to go out on loan, and they can't sign that contract until they are 17 years old. Salmon doesn't turn 17 until August 29, meaning that there will be just a few days for Arsenal to sort out a loan deal if they decide to send him out for valuable game time.

View 4 Images Marli Salmon staked his case for more involvement

It will be less complicated for Theo Julienne, who made his first pre-season appearance by starting at left-back. The 18-year-old didn’t look out of place, but a loan deal and regular game time this season may benefit him.

‌



Ethan Nwaneri chance

Ethan Nwaneri is another player who may have been playing for a place in the starting XI for the season opener against Coventry City in under two weeks.

Competition for places means that in the number 10 role Nwaneri has Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard vying for the same spot.

Article continues below

With Declan Rice still not back after the World Cup, Nwaneri was given the chance to impress in a slightly deeper role. Lewis-Skelly sitting allowed him to go forward and help Eze in the number 10 role; there was then more of an interchange when Fabio Vieira was introduced after half an hour.

He caught the eye in the opening stages, often playing a big role in the high press, which led to some early chances. He did, however, fade as the half went on and was replaced by Guimaraes at halftime.

Sports.title: Man Utd frustrated by Leeds as Bruno Fernandes reminder sent - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Manchester United and Leeds couldn't be separated despite both having chances to win their pre-season clash in Dublin.

In a game that eventually saw the two sides throw on their headline names, neither of them could find the goal that would've given one side bragging rights over the other with just one outing left before the Premier League season begins.

Joshua Zirkzee was on hand to score the game's opener after some impressive work from Bryan Mbeumo, who was among the game's outstanding players. He waltzed past his opposite number and had half of Croke Park to run into, before laying on his team-mate to finish past James Trafford.

Despite United's dominance it was Leeds who were able to claw their way back into the game, thanks to a lapse in concentration, which allowed Dan James to get hold of the ball before laying on Brenden Aaronson to score.

Mbeumo would see a shot hit the bar just before the break and, once the second-half got underway, Senne Lammens needed to produce a reaction save to deny Harry Wilson.

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

By the time the hour mark hit 20 of the 22 players on the pitch had appeared from the bench. But even with Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha pulling the strings the Red Devils couldn't find the winner. The Portuguese star did have the ball in the net before the offside flag denied him and hit the bar in the dying stages as his quality showed, but couldn't provide the winning touch.

Determined to give the thousands of fans a winner, the Boyle Sports Cup went to penalties, and Fernandes' failure to hit the target silenced the stadium. The shootout went beyond the five spot kicks and the unlucky man to miss was James Justin - handing those from Manchester the trophy. Here's five talking points from the Irish capital.

Lack of cutting edge frustrates Red Devils

Across the course of the evening those in red will certainly say they had more possession and time in the final third, but it counts for little if you can't make it count. Alex Cairns came on for James Trafford at half-time, but will not have expected to be so rarely called upon.

View 4 Images Joshua Zirkzee's future is still unclear but he scored the game's opener

If anything it was Dermott Mee who needed to make the more notable saves in the second-half. United were minus Benjamin Sesko, who will look to truly establish himself as the team's striker this season, and a No 9 on form may well have seized on some of the half chances that were created. Fernandes, as he has done some many times, tried to win the match with individual bits of quality, but fell just short. The United talisman was able to smile after his penalty miss, which he'll hope is the only blot on his record this season.

Zirkzee hushes talk of exit

The Dutchman hasn't lit up Old Trafford during his two years at the club, so much so that his days could be numbered amid talk of a return to Italy, possibly with Juventus. He's seen forwards arrive and push him down the pecking order but he was tasked with leading the line and needed less than 20 minutes to score the opener.

Zirkzee profited from some impressive play from Mbeumo, but his first time finish was of a player in confidence. This close to the season managers often look to get players who are going to be part of their plans match sharp - and the Dutchman looks that, even if his future remains unclear.

Leeds ring the changes as depth on show

The Whites came out for the second-half, albeit later than they should, with a team featuring 10 news players as Daniel Farke changed all but one individual. If anything Leeds' side looked better than it did in the opening 45 minutes as Anton Stach, Ethan Ampadu, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and new signing Wilson all ran out.

View 4 Images Brenden Aaronson had Leeds level by half-time

It serves to highlight how, after two summer transfer windows, Leeds have created a squad that looks more capable of dealing with life in the top flight. They won the Championship in 2025 but already have been able to attract the likes of Wilson, who was not short of offers this summer. If the feared second season is about to begin, they look more than equipped for it.

Fletcher's timely reminder

In an area where United want to level up, Tyler Fletcher will learn quickly that notable errors could stick in the mind of his bosses. The teenager is set for more involvement this season, but a lapse in contentration in his own third just seconds before Leeds' equaliser will serve as a frustration.

Central midfield is a position which has already seen two new faces arrive, another could follow, and Fletcher will know that taking risks, failing to look over your shoulder, won't fly once the competitive games come round. The 19-year-old has made plenty of forward strides in pre-season, but Aaronson's equaliser will serve as a reminder of how quickly a mistake can be punished.

View 4 Images Both teams will play once more before the Premier League begins in less than a fortnight

Rivalry in full swing

82,000 packed out Croke Park, Europe's third biggest stadium, and further served to highlight how healthy the Yorkshire vs Lancashire rivalry is. When you consider the two teams didn't play each other in the league for 16 years, the passion for the match-up has more than remained.

Leeds secured a landmark victory at Old Trafford last year, one of the few defeats Michael Carrick had to stomach, and the county divide coupled with years of history ensures that this remains one of England's most hotly contest affairs - and that doesn't change when they cross the Irish Sea.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'
Sports.content:
Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'

Manchester United have been linked with Leicester City's Louis Page but Russell Martin has made it clear the teenager is not for sale

View 2 Images Man Utd are eyeing up a move for Leicester's Louis Page (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Leicester boss Russell Martin admits he'd tell Manchester United chief Jason Wilcox "to go away" if he made attempts to sign teenager Louis Page.

‌



The 18-year-old was named the EFL Apprentice of the Year last season and is seen as one of the most exciting talents in the Football League - attracting attention from the Red Devils.

‌



Page would reportedly be keen on moving to Old Trafford if the opportunity arose, but Leicester are determined to keep hold of their academy graduate. The England U20 international has already made 21 senior appearances for the Foxes - including five starts last season. He played in their Carabao Cup win over Northampton on Saturday.

‌



Martin has been appointed as the Foxes new boss following their relegation to League One and he previously worked at Southampton with Wilcox, who is now the director of football at United. He admits, despite their history, he'd tell him to look elsewhere if they came looking for Page.

Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message READ MORE :

Youri Tielemans sends clear Marcus Rashford message to Michael Carrick after Man Utd reunion READ MORE :

He jokingly told Sky Sports: "Louis is a really fantastic young player. Obviously, I know the director of football at Manchester United very well after spending some time with Southampton. So we haven't actually spoken with Louis because he probably knows what I'd say to him and tell him to go away.

"But no, until something comes in that is really brilliant for the club, the player, and everyone is happy, then Louis stays, and he's in the squad. I'm really enjoying working with him. He's a fantastic young player."

‌



View 2 Images Leicester's teenage star recently signed a professional deal

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also shown an interest in Page. Leicester have already lost one of their leading young prospects this summer after seeing forward Jeremy Monga, 17, join Manchester City, and they will be loathed to see another leave the King Power Stadium.

Page signed professional terms with the Foxes in September last year, which means United would need to agree a transfer fee if they wanted to secure his services.

Article continues below

Leicester said after he penned his deal: "After joining us at Under-9s, Louis has progressed through our Academy ranks and developed within the LCFC pathway into one of the brightest talents in our system".

Sports.title: MI London's Hundred title defence over despite narrow win over Phoenix
Sports.content:
MI London had the lights turned out on their hopes of claiming a fourth straight Hundred title despite beating bottom-placed Birmingham Phoenix in a nip-and-tuck final men's group match.

As the Edgbaston crowd were treated to a solar eclipse, the visitors knew they needed to win by at least 59 runs to take third position from SunRisers Leeds and qualify for the play-off on their home patch after Phoenix won a crucial toss and elected to field.

A total of 157-6 meant they would progress if they could restrict Phoenix to 98, and three wickets in the powerplay put a spring in their step, Sikandar Raza clean bowling Joe Clarke and Richard Gleeson dismissing Mitchell Owen and Laurie Evans with consecutive deliveries to pull clear as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 14 victims.

However, a solid partnership between Jake Weatherley and Sean Dickson steadied the ship and a Tom Curran wide took Phoenix to 99 and ended MI London's slim hopes.

Dickson (23 from 17) fell lbw to Sam Curran, who then had Weatherley (42 from 31) caught in the deep as the hosts lost momentum but Jordan Thompson (23no from 13) and Rehan Ahmed (23 from 11) took them close before Trent Boult held his nerve, nailing his late yorkers to seal a two-run victory.

Earlier, Will Jacks had made a positive start for MI London before falling to Chris Wood after slicing to deep point. James Vince looked in good touch and Nicholas Pooran announced his arrival by dispatching Tom Helm for 10 runs in two deliveries, but Helm came back to bowl Vince (22 off 12) with a back-of-the-hand slowie.

Rehan then put the brakes on by deceiving Sam Curran with a googly and conceded just three runs from his first 10 deliveries, including six consecutive dots.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad reveal their choices for best local player in The Hundred men's competition, best captain and more!

Thompson took the key wicket of Pooran (36 from 21) when the Trinidadian holed out to long-off before Jason Roy (26 off 21) became Rehan's second victim. Curiously, boasting figures of 2-7 from 15 balls, the leg-spinner was not called upon to complete his quota.

Raza (17 from 13), Ollie Sykes (23no off 14) on debut and Tom Curran (17no off 9) played useful cameos but MI London's total never looked sufficient to produce the miracle they needed.

With the reigning champions eliminated from the competition, SunRisers Leeds will now play Manchester Super Giants on Friday evening at The Kia Oval, with the prize of a Lord's final against Trent Rockets at stake.

Gleeson said: "To win five games and not qualify when two teams have done the same as us is disappointing, but that shows the strength of the competition and you've got to be on top of your game all the way through - 30, 40, 50 runs can make a big difference."

Welsh Fire and London Spirit's men's teams found themselves in similar positions to their female counterparts - unable to qualify for The Hundred eliminator at The Oval on Friday, let alone Sunday's final at Lord's.

Qualification was statistically possible for Fire but it would have meant a record-breaking margin of victory, their four wins having been close affairs and their losses heavy ones.

But that did not mean a lack of competitive spirit in front of a boisterous Cardiff crowd as the Spirit manfully defended 131 to claim a third win of the campaign.

Fire chose to bowl after winning the toss. And that decision paid off initially, Chris Woakes showing his enduring brilliance up front in shackling the powerful pairing of Jonny Bairstow and Lhuan-dre Pretorius, allowing Lockie Ferguson to benefit from the pressure applied by picking up the South African the ball after he had him dropped.

A score of 34-1 from the powerplay with Bairstow on 22 from 11, was an inconclusive start. Twenty-five balls later and it was 59-3, with the Fire in the ascendancy, Woakes having got rid of Bairstow for 34 from 19, Marco Jansen having bowled 10 dot balls in his first 15.

Liam Livingstone and Dewald Brevis, Spirit's leading run-scorers in the tournament with 233 and 212, both went cheaply, and James Coles, belatedly growing into the tournament, flickered for 29 until all 6ft 8in of Jansen leapt at long-off to flick the ball back in for Tom Kohler-Cadmore to complete the catch.

When Fire batted, they lost Matt Short immediately but Phil Salt and Joe Root cruised along, the feeling that wickets in the bank chasing a middling target would be enough.

At 90-2 off 69 balls, with Jordan Cox flexing his muscles, that thinking seemed sound but the glue disappeared with Root (31 from 31) and Cox (44 from 28). Kohler-Cadmore, Ravindra and Jansen disappeared in the last eight balls to leave the Fire just one hit away, losing by six runs.

Sports.title: Rashford absent in Leeds friendly win but still part of Man Utd plans
Sports.content:
Joshua Zirkzee and Brenden Aaronson scored as Manchester United and old foes Leeds played out an entertaining 1-1 friendly draw at the spiritual home of Irish sport in Dublin, before the concluding shoot-out was edged 5-4 by Michael Carrick's side.

On the eve of the new Premier League season, all the talk was about Marcus Rashford and his reintegration under Carrick, but the 82,000-strong crowd at Croke Park were not treated to a first glimpse of the forward in a Man Utd shirt for over 18 months.

Carrick did hint, however, that he intends to keep Rashford around after he returned from his Old Trafford hiatus in "great spirits", adding "he gives us something a bit different".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Kahn runs through the key talking points from Manchester United's pre-season clash with Leeds United.

The Man Utd boss also kept a number of other high-profile stars in reserve until after the hour mark, instead choosing to give a raft of youngsters a proper run-out. Full-back Harry Amass turned out to be the pick of the rookie pack.

The introduction of Bruno Fernandes and new signing Youri Tielemans improved efficiencies late on, combining effectively to offer Matheus Cunha some pre-season shooting practice, adding to a lively attacking performance from the lesser-seen Zirkzee.

Fernandes himself was played through by Luke Shaw in the second period, much to the delight of the pro-Manchester United fanbase, who chanted 'Bruno, Bruno, Bruno' for large portions of the night, but his strike was flagged offside. He also hammered the crossbar late on.

Image: Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin heads at goal

Of those senior regulars who did start, Bryan Mbeumo caught the eye, showing impressive intensity to tee-up Zirkzee for the game's opener. Dan James and Aaronson were Leeds' conspirators shortly after to turn home their first of five shots on target. Daniel Farke's side have scored a tidy 10 goals in five pre-season outings this summer, albeit they lacked a little composure in the decisive shoot-out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Marcus Rashford recently returned to Manchester United's training ground ahead of the new season, after a loan spell at Barcelona. Credit: @rachaelandimogenmufc.

The key moments from Croke Park

16: GOAL! Joshua Zirkzee sweeps home a smart, low cross from Bryan Mbeumo.

29: GOAL! Dan James latches onto a punt from James Trafford and baits Ayden Heaven before feeding Brenden Aaronson to equalise.

46: SUBS! Leeds change the majority of their starting XI, with Harry Wilson, Dom Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor among those introduced.

60: SUBS! Michael Carrick sends on Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans and Matheus Cunha.

80: RULED OUT! Fernandes' strike is chalked off after the offside flag is raised. He crashes an effort off the crossbar not long after.

PENALTIES! Wilson missed first for Leeds, but was reprieved when Fernandes also spurned his opportunity. James Justin's miss proved decisive as Noussair Mazraoui netted the winner.

Carrick: Rashford gives us point of difference

Michael Carrick on the return of Marcus Rashford:

"He's our player. He's come back great. I've known Marcus a long time, he offers us something a bit different.

"He's trained only two or three days and it's all normal. He's come back in great spirits. We're looking forward to the start of the season."

Farke: Trafford can be world-class

Daniel Farke on new Leeds signing James Trafford:

"He has the potential to be world-class. If he keeps going like this he will rise to the top.

"We have a feeling he can make a big difference, a top-class No 1 is crucial for the club and I pushed very hard for this transfer. I'm very happy. It was a good debut, we're all delighted to have him."

What comes next?

Sports.title: Guimaraes makes bow and Lewis-Skelly scores as Arsenal held by Como
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes made his first appearance and Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid speculation about his future as Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Como before winning 4-3 on penalties.

Guimaraes, a £75m signing from Newcastle, was introduced at half-time in the pre-season friendly at the Emirates Stadium after Lewis-Skelly's opener had been cancelled out by Martin Baturina.

Lewis-Skelly's goal, stroked home after cutting out a poor pass from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez, came as he is linked with an Arsenal exit. He celebrated by making a heart gesture with his hands.

Guimaraes received a warm welcome with his introduction but Arsenal were unable to find a second-half winner before emerging victorious in the post-match penalty shoot-out in which Guimaraes and fellow new signing Christos Tzolis were among the scorers.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes came on at half-time

Mikel Arteta left out Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi despite their returns from World Cup duty this week, but there were first cameos of pre-season from their England and Spain team-mates Eberechi Eze, David Raya, Mikel Merino and Noni Madueke.

Arsenal's attention now turns to Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City at Wembley before their Premier League curtain-raiser against Coventry, live on Sky Sports, on Friday August 21.

The key moments from the Emirates Stadium

7: CHANCE! Gabriel Jesus misses a sitter as his shot hits the post when it appeared easier to score.

Gabriel Jesus misses a sitter as his shot hits the post when it appeared easier to score. 21: SAVE! Martin Baturina cuts inside from the left flank and forces a low save from Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Martin Baturina cuts inside from the left flank and forces a low save from Kepa Arrizabalaga. 33: GOAL! Myles Lewis-Skelly punishes an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez as he strokes home the opener

Myles Lewis-Skelly punishes an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez as he strokes home the opener 43: GOAL! Como pull level as Baturina dances between Theo Julienne and Max Dowman before firing home an emphatic finish.

Como pull level as Baturina dances between Theo Julienne and Max Dowman before firing home an emphatic finish. 46: WELCOME! Bruno Guimaraes is welcomed by the home fans as he is introduced at half-time for his first Gunners appearance.

Bruno Guimaraes is welcomed by the home fans as he is introduced at half-time for his first Gunners appearance. 53 WASTE! Martin Odegaard puts a chance on a plate for Fabio Vieira but his shot is saved.

Martin Odegaard puts a chance on a plate for Fabio Vieira but his shot is saved. PENALTIES! Arsenal win the shoot-out 4-3 with Guimaraes among the scorers and Noni Madueke the only player to miss.

Analysis: Salmon shows star potential

The debut of a £75m signing and a goal from the player who may have to make way for his arrival took the headlines, but the performance from Marli Salmon provided another talking point.

One of two Arsenal 16-year-olds to start the game along with Max Dowman, the defender was outstanding, his performance a continuation of a strong pre-season.

He lined up at centre-back, with another teenager, the 18-year-old Theo Julienne, as his full-back, but as Arteta made sweeping substitutions and the personnel around him changed, Salmon remained calm and consistent, earning a standing ovation from fans inside the ground when he finally came off in the 88th minute.

Image: Marli Salmon and Mikel Arteta

Salmon departed having won nine of his 13 duels, the most of any player on either side. He had also completed 42 of his 43 passes, which was, again, a game high. The numbers reflected his confidence and quality both in and out of possession.

Como head coach Cesc Fabregas, himself a former Arsenal academy prodigy, marvelled at his impact alongside Dowman. "Amazing. That's what it's all about. Hale End does an amazing job," he said. And there was also praise from Arteta, who appears to have another credible defensive option. "I think he was exceptional," he said.

Arteta: Bruno was pushing to play

Manager Mikel Arteta on Bruno Guimaraes in his press conference: "He only had three training sessions, but he looked good.

"He was really pushing to play some minutes today.

"I think he wanted to get his debut and the feeling of playing in front of our fans immediately.

"And, yeah, you sense immediately, I believe, a strong connection at play that is going to make us better."

Merino: We're ready for 'another final'

Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino speaking to Arsenal's official YouTube channel: "I think we dominated. The team showed what it is capable of.

"Everyone was in a good level. Honestly, I think we deserved to win; we had massive chances to score.

"We take the positives into the next game and hopefully we can dominate every game like we did today."

On the Community Shield: "It's another final and we want to win, we want to give the fans more happiness.

"But especially for us, we want to compete. Wearing this shirt and this badge means a lot and that's about giving everything and playing to our best capacity."

August 12: Arsenal 1-1 Como

Sports.title: Arteta: There's more we want to do in the transfer market
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are actively looking for more new signings in the transfer market but admits there is only a small pool of available players who can take them to the next level.

The Gunners were frustrated in their attempts to land Vinicius Junior, who chose to sign a new contract at Real Madrid, and also missed out on the signing of another top target Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea from Aston Villa earlier this summer.

Arsenal completed the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes on Saturday, with the Brazil international making his first appearance for the club in Wednesday's friendly against Como at the Emirates Stadium, but their efforts to add firepower are ongoing.

"There is more that we want to do because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that," said Arteta.

"We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.

"But the approach, the will and the desire of the club, that's unquestionable. We want to try to do that. But we cannot promise that we're going to do it because it doesn't only depend on us."

The Premier League champions are interested in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola but their search for a marquee attacking signing appears set to continue deep into the transfer window.

"I think for the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring that to the club," added Arteta.

"But again, we are actively looking to improve that and we're going to try."

Asked if Arsenal's wage structure could be affected by signings of that stature, Arteta added: "I'll leave that question to [sporting director] Andrea [Berta] and the board.

"My job is more to focus on getting the best out of the players that we have, to create that connection between them and to make every player feel important, regardless of the wages."

'Bruno was pushing to play'

Arteta was pleased to hand a debut to Guimaraes against Como. The midfielder impressed as a half-time substitute, only four days after his arrival from Newcastle, and could now be in contention to start Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes featured in the second half against Como

"Let's see," said Arteta. "He only had three training sessions, but he looked good. He was really pushing to play some minutes.

"I think he wanted to get his debut and the feeling of playing in front of our fans immediately.

"And you sense immediately, I believe, a strong connection at play that is going to make us better."

Arteta coy on Lewis-Skelly future

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a departure from Arsenal following the arrival of Guimaraes. He was the subject of an enquiry from Chelsea and is also a long-term target for Manchester United.

But the 19-year-old scored Arsenal's goal against Como, after which he made a heart gesture before holding his hands together towards the home fans.

Image: Myles Lewis-Skelly gestured to Arsenal fans after his goal

"It's good to score a goal, you should be emotional when you score a goal," said Arteta of his celebration. "He's a very emotional player. I remember when he did all the gestures on the pitch [last season]. I'm not going to talk about any speculation.

"If there is a speculation about our player, it's a good sign. That means that we attract attention and they're doing a good job.

"I think he had a really good pre-season. I think we asked him to play in a different position, because he played more as a six, because we lacked central midfielders, obviously with international duties, and I think he had a really consistent pre-season."

Sports.title: Chelsea set Man City deadline to bid for Fernandez
Sports.content:
Chelsea have told Manchester City they have a deadline of 5pm this Friday to make an offer for Enzo Fernandez.

City are interested in the midfielder, who shared a strong relationship with Enzo Maresca when he was Chelsea boss.

Chelsea value Fernandez at £120m and he has six years left on his contract.

If City do not meet Chelsea's demands, they do not intend to sell Fernandez in this window.

Barcelona's pursuit of Rodri - which saw them have a £40m bid rejected - has raised the prospect of Manchester City making a late move for Fernandez before the window closes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Mark McAdam with the latest on Rodri's potential move to LaLiga side Barcelona

City have targets in mind for any player who departs and they are in ongoing talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi. They have already signed central-midfielder Elliot Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest.

Chelsea have a high valuation for Fernandez but they signed him for around £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window. The summer transfer window closes on Tuesday September 1.

Relations between City and Chelsea are strained after the acrimonious manner of Maresca's departure from Chelsea.

City paid Chelsea £17m in compensation to appoint Maresca this summer. He had resigned with three and a half years to run on his contract at the end of 2025 after being sounded out about succeeding Pep Guardiola last autumn.

Chelsea chose to impose this deadline to avoid the distractions that arose when Maresca stood down with his shock exit announced by the club on New Year's Day.

Their view is that interested clubs have had the best part of two months to make an approach for Fernandez. They want new manager Xabi Alonso and his players to be able to focus on the new season ahead.

Fernandez was dropped by Chelsea for two games in April after he admitted he would welcome living in Madrid.

The player and his agent also apologised for his comments. They had been seeking improved terms at Chelsea.

Real Madrid released a statement earlier this summer denying that they would make an attempt to sign Fernandez.

Barcelona expected to raise bid for Rodri

Barcelona are ready to raise their offer for Rodri - which could lead to Man City making their move for Fernandez before Chelsea's deadline.

City want to keep the 30-year-old but he has entered the final year of his contract.

Barcelona are ready to up their offer to City for Rodri to somewhere in the £50m (€60m) to £60m (€70m) bracket.

City are also aware of interest from Nottingham Forest in Tijjani Reijnders.

Sports.title: Atletico agree deal to sign Spurs captain Romero
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle with Tottenham to sign Cristian Romero.

The package is in the region of £34.2m (€40m) with add-ons. A 15 per cent sell-on clause is included.

Atletico have been long-term admirers of the Argentina international, and there was an expectation that Spurs would allow captain Romero to depart this summer if the right offer arrived.
