The central defender was always believed to have preferred a move to Atletico, with Inter Milan and Spurs' north London rivals Arsenal among the other clubs to have been interested.

Romero's Spurs deal is due to run until the summer of 2029.

The 28-year-old was sent off twice last season during Spurs' Premier League relegation battle. He then missed the end of the campaign due to a knee injury.

Romero received criticism from supporters when he appeared to be set to watch his boyhood club Belgrano play River Plate in the Argentina Primera Division Apertura final instead of being at Tottenham's crucial last game against Everton. Romero did, though, attend the final game of the season, in which Spurs secured Premier League survival.

He has made 124 appearances for the club over five seasons, scoring 12 goals and being shown four red cards in the Premier League.

Spurs had appeared to lay the groundwork for Romero's exit this summer following the arrivals of defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

'Spurs not getting value for Romero'

Spurs are set to take a lower fee for Romero than what they received for teenage defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined Brighton in a club-record £50m deal earlier this summer.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, which will be available to listen to from midday on Thursday, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge said of Romero's imminent exit: "Spurs are not going to get the value for a player of his ability.

"Luka Vuskovic, who didn't make any competitive appearances for Spurs, will be sold for more than what the club's captain will go for because he's gone to a Premier League club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Romero's last game for Spurs ended in tears as he suffered a season-ending injury in the loss at Sunderland

"I think it's best for all parties that Romero leaves. I think 99.9 per cent of Spurs fans would agree with that.

"On his day, there aren't many better - he doesn't make any mistakes for Argentina, but in terms of Tottenham it just feels like it's his job.

"He adores Argentina, and there's nothing wrong with that, but it feels as if Tottenham is a bit of a chore for him and it's gone a bit too much that way."

Could Romero have joined Arsenal?

Earlier this month, one source had told Sky Sports News that Arsenal had looked into Romero as an option to bolster their centre-back options.

However, it never progressed beyond interest, with Spurs reluctant to let their captain join a Premier League side, let alone their fiercest rivals Arsenal.

"There was talk that Romero would have happily accepted a move to Arsenal," Bridge told Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast.

"There were no club-to-club talks on this, but when you hear that then that's the final nail for Tottenham supporters."

The north London rivals tend not to do transfer business with one another. The last transfer negotiated between the two clubs came 49 years ago when goalkeeper Pat Jennings joined Arsenal from Spurs in a deal worth a reported £45,000.

O'Hara: Time for Romero to move on

Also speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, ex-Spurs midfielder Jamie O'Hara said of Romero: "He's a bit of a liability. When he plays, he costs us games, points and red cards.

"I just think his attitude towards the board and the way he was, I just think it's, 'All right, thank you, and we're going to move on'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara called for Tottenham to sell Romero

"We've finished 17th the last two seasons, and he's been involved. He was captain last season, and the way he acted at the end of the season, when he got injured, and we all saw him crying, that wasn't for Tottenham; it was more for Argentina and his World Cup.

"And then he goes to Argentina on the last day of the season, and everyone's like, 'Where's Romero?' So that situation for me needs to be put to bed. I don't think we need any of that bad publicity around us.

"Get as much as we can for him; let him move on. We've got back-up now with Van Hecke and Senesi, so thank you, see you later."

Spurs are set to make a loss on Romero, who joined from Atalanta for around £42m in the summer of 2021.

O'Hara said of Atletico's £34.2m deal for Romero: "The problem is there's a premium for English clubs, who will pay over the odds for people with European clubs inflating the fee.

"The problem is if you're going to go and sell him to Atletico Madrid, they haven't got the money.

"If we were selling him to Man Utd, we could probably get £60m-70m for him. But the problem is if you sell a player to Europe, they just don't have the money that the Premier League clubs have, so you have to accept that it's going to be a lesser fee than what maybe you think you can get for him.

"He wants to go to Atletico Madrid. He just feels like an Atletico Madrid player. I just feel like you've just got to take that one on the chin and move on from it."

Romero's exit signals new era at Spurs

Image: Romero is set to leave Spurs after five years at the club

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, Sky Sports News senior football news editor Lyall Thomas said:

"Quite a top figure in the football industry said to me, 'Go and watch Romero's role in the second goal in Spurs' 3-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest at home last season'.

"I watched him, and it was arms in the air, not tracking the player back who ended up scoring, which contributed to the goal.

"That was Spurs when they needed their captain the most, and he just wasn't there in that moment, so that says it all.

"It's time to move on from that era of Spurs and into the new era.

"This has been shown by some of the players they've brought in, which is not just to have an impact on the field but to have an impact on the dressing room and sort that area of the club.

"It's a move that suits Romero to go and work with his compatriot [Diego] Simeone. I can imagine they will suit each other down to the ground. It just fits. The planets are aligned on this one."

Sports.title: Doue silences Madjo-mania as PSG beat Villa to win Super Cup
Sports.content:
Desire Doue scored the winner as champions of Europe Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup.

The 21-year-old raced in behind the defence and restored the lead for the Ligue 1 side to ensure they retained the trophy but Villa went down swinging in what was a highly-contested fixture at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had initially given PSG the lead after cutting inside from the left and wrong-footing Marco Bizot with his well-taken effort (20) but a goal on his professional debut for 17-year-old Brian Madjo sparked Villa into life.

The forward became the youngest player to score in the Super Cup after shrugging off the challenge from Willian Pacho to volley the equaliser home and arguably should have had more to his name, having seen three other chances sail just wide of the target.

Image: Brian Madjo of Aston Villa celebrates scoring against PSG

Villa were without key players Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emiliano Martinez due to their extended post-World Cup breaks but the gaps left by senior players provided the likes of Madjo and 19-year-old George Hemmings with a platform to shine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyrone Mings and Matty Cash were full of praise for 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who became the youngest-ever goal scorer in Super Cup history in Aston Villa's loss to PSG.

The two teenagers looked at home among world-class opposition and the latter came close to responding to Doue's strike seconds after Villa conceded, only for Matvey Safonov to make a fine stop to deny him.

Image: Desire Doue celebrates after scoring what proved the winner for PSG against Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup

Luis Enrique's side would hold on to start the 2026/27 campaign with silverware but they were given an almighty scare by Unai Emery and his new-look squad, in a similar fashion to the 5-4 thriller that played out in the Champions League when the sides last met in 2025.

The key moments from Red Bull Arena Salzburg

20: GOAL! Kvaratskhelia opens the scoring for PSG

Kvaratskhelia opens the scoring for PSG 28: CLOSE! Madjo's header curls just wide of the target

Madjo's header curls just wide of the target 35: MADJO MISSES! Another shot from the young striker whistles just wide

Another shot from the young striker whistles just wide 41: MADJO HAS TO SCORE! Madjo's header balloons over the bar from close range

Madjo's header balloons over the bar from close range 45: FINALLY! Madjo makes history and becomes youngest Super Cup goalscorer

Madjo makes history and becomes youngest Super Cup goalscorer 62: GOAL! Doue restores PSG lead

Doue restores PSG lead 64: SAVE! Hemmings has chance to equalise but Safonov saves

Emery: We must feel proud of this performance

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to TNT Sports:

"With a loss, you can never feel happy but how we compete, how the players respond on the field for 90 minutes. And our chances to score, we must feel really very proud of what we have done today."

On the performances of Brian Madjo and George Hemmings: "Their experiences and having days like today are very important.

"They show how are they are learning after their hard work. This is the way. We decided before the game how we wanted to play this game; we have worked the players in these positions."

Sports.title: Doué seals Super Cup glory for PSG after Madjo makes history for Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique says it doesn’t matter which sport he is playing – football, tennis, padel or parchis, a board game – he wants to win all of the time. In Paris Saint-Germain, he has built a winning machine, the back-to-back Champions League victors maintaining a useful habit by conquering Aston Villa in an absorbing Super Cup contest in Salzburg. For PSG, after the joy of Munich and Budapest, three months ago, does a three-peat in Madrid in May beckon?

Aston Villa more than played their part in an enthralling showpiece, Brian Madjo becoming the competition’s youngest scorer after the 17-year-old cancelled out Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s opener. They could have taken the game to a penalty shootout, Warren Zaïre-Emery’s extraordinary block preventing João Gomes a near-certain debut goal and Emi Buendía heading wide in stoppage time.

Villa will take plenty of encouragement from a fearless display, Désiré Doué’s well-taken winner ultimately the difference. The goal was initially disallowed but, after a VAR review, Omar Artan – the Somali referee handed the game by Uefa after being denied entry to the US to officiate at the World Cup – awarded it after replays showed Matty Cash played Doué onside.

Before kick-off, the sights and sounds were in effect an extension of Villa’s victory in Istanbul, a party atmosphere raining down from the 6,000-strong Villa following. There were huge cheers when Unai Emery’s face appeared on the big screens in opposite corners after the teams were read aloud and hearty roars for the £38m arrival Gomes and Madjo, the hulking forward who made his presence felt on his full Villa debut. Madjo’s inclusion felt particularly ominous for Tammy Abraham, the striker signed seven months ago, his £18.25m arrival yet to pay dividends.

“We won’t be in our best moment,” Emery warned on the eve of the game but, after a summer of change, the future looks bright. Emery could finally unleash Madjo in a competitive game for the first time since his £10m arrival from Metz in January, Villa winning an appeal at the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) to register him after Fifa prohibited him from playing. Chelsea’s João Pedro is the only Premier League player to have outscored Madjo in pre-season and his equaliser here was on the grandest stage yet after goals against Walsall, Real Sociedad and Indonesia All Stars. Madjo occupied Willian Pacho and Marquinhos, one of the most decorated defenders in the world. The 19-year-old George Hemmings played the full game and kept Achraf Hakimi on his toes.

Only five players from Villa’s memorable victory over Freiburg remained in the XI though Emi Martínez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins are still on holiday. Emery told Watkins to rest after the striker volunteered to play here. Boubacar Kamara made his first start since sustaining a serious knee injury against Tottenham in January. More new faces will join, with Villa in advanced talks to sign João Palhinha from Bayern Munich and the Atlético Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri expected to undergo a medical in the next 48 hours. “Overall we can feel proud of everything we’ve done,” Emery said. “Some changes will be needed but we are confident.”

View image in fullscreen Brian Madjo punches the air after scoring for Aston Villa on the stroke of half-time. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

PSG seized the lead on 20 minutes through Kvaratskhelia, who had the summer off. Madjo’s clunky control allowed Vitinha to claim the ball and locate Doué. Then Kvaratskhelia took charge, jinking inside Cash and blasting his shot in at Marco Bizot’s near post. Six minutes later, it should have been 2-0 after more Kvaratskhelia brilliance, but PSG could not apply the finishing touch. Nuno Mendes galloped on to Kvaratskhelia’s flipped pass but the full-back’s cutback from the left flank evaded the £43m summer buy Maghnes Akliouche and three other blue and red shirts.

Madjo had a hat-trick of chances from John McGinn’s cunning crosses before levelling. He glanced at the screens showing a replay of him misdirecting a free header. Then he overcooked a shot when looking for the far corner after Hemmings beat Hakimi. Another flunked header followed after McGinn twirled clear of Kvaratskhelia. But with the half-time whistle looming, Madjo made amends, dispatching a side-footed volley into the roof of Matvey Safonov’s net after meeting another brilliant cross from McGinn. As the ball flew towards the back post, Pacho clung to Madjo for dear life, but the teenager kept him at arm’s length to ripple the net.

Ousmane Dembélé replaced Akliouche at half-time. Fabián Ruiz, the only other player missing from the XI that began against Arsenal in Budapest in May, arrived late on. Villa kept hunting, McGinn working Safonov after Madjo spread play. But PSG regained the lead just after the hour when Dembélé’s pass unlocked Villa’s defence, exposing an imperfect offside line. Dembélé zipped the ball into the right channel and, while Ian Maatsen and Pau Torres raised their hands and Doué’s goal was initially ruled out, semi-automated offside exposed Cash.

Villa still had chances to level. Zaïre-Emery slid across the turf to thwart Gomes. Safonov repelled Hemmings’s strike from close range and the substitutes Alysson and Abraham almost combined to devastating effect but Abraham did not gamble in the box, much to Emery’s frustration. Perhaps Villa will, as McGinn suggested this week, prove everybody wrong – again.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 7: Coventry
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 18th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st (Championship)

Prospects

“We are back”, as the banners proudly state. It is 25 years since, after relegation was confirmed, Match of the Day cameras lingered on a message held aloft by a Coventry City supporter named John Mullaney. “We’ll be back,” were the words he inked – in sky blue, of course – on a scrap of wallpaper. When Coventry celebrated returning to the top flight and lifted the Championship trophy in front of a capacity crowd, thousands of supporters held aloft new-look signs with a tweaked slogan to symbolise the journey coming full circle: “We are back”.

It has not been without pain along the way; nine years ago they were preparing for their first season in the fourth tier for 59 years, and from 2019 to 2021 they had to share St Andrew’s with the landlords Birmingham. That was not even their first spell of homelessness; in 2013-14, they played “home” games 35 miles away in Northampton. Many supporters will recall those harder times when Frank Lampard’s side kick off the new season in the Premier League curtain-raiser at champions Arsenal a week on Friday. Many will also remember the work of Mark Robins, who across two spells spent more than eight years in charge, en route to this point.

The biggest challenge will be adapting to the level. Lampard is a Premier League great but only seven of his squad count experience of the division on their CVs, the returning maverick Gus Hamer boasting the most starts among them (34) from his season in the top flight with Sheffield United. “Part of that is a good thing: we’re excited, hungry and the players want to show they deserve to be here,” Lampard said. “But we also have to work to help the squad to bridge the gap.”

Coventry’s recruitment has been superb under the sporting director, Dean Austin, and the club-record £23m arrival of Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi from the Danish side FC Nordsjælland is particularly exciting. Some of those who flourished upon joining in the second tier also look capable of stepping up, including Milan van Ewijk, Jack Rudoni and Carl Rushworth, who has signed permanently after a successful loan from Brighton. Goals were no problem last season: Coventry were the highest scorers in English football’s top four tiers with 97.

Aside from a playoff semi-final defeat to Sunderland last year and a bumpy start to this one, it has been largely smooth sailing since Lampard succeeded Robins in November 2024. Coventry lost seven league matches last season, only two at home, and the going will be tougher in the top tier. “We’ve won a lot of games at this club in the last year – it’s going to be much harder to do that in the Premier League,” Lampard said. “I’m not scared of that. We have to be excited by it.”

Off-field picture

Coventry launched a “storytelling space” at the club’s stadium to celebrate promotion and the path to this point. The first exhibition in the club’s museum is titled The Journey Back, which tells the club’s story from homelessness to the Premier League and showcases artefacts donated by supporters, players and managers and the owner, Doug King, opened last month. Promotion means abiding by Premier League regulations and the Coventry Building Society Arena, as it is now known, has dropped in capacity by about 300 seats in order to accommodate camera gantries and other changes to ensure compliance.

Owner-fan relationship

King angered supporters when sacking Robins but his decision was ultimately vindicated. King is never too proud to get involved: see him fist pumping the crowd, belting out the Enemy’s We’ll Live and Die in These Towns, the club’s de facto pre-match anthem, from the directors’ box, or swaying to Take That, who performed a trio of gigs at the stadium he bought 12 months ago – another big tick. Such is King’s popularity, supporters chant his name and a couple last season donned fancy dress to masquerade as him, wearing lanyards, sky-blue ties and bouffant wigs. “They tried to blag themselves into the boardroom ... but I’m way more handsome than them,” King said.

The manager

Promotion to the Premier League, Lampard says, marked the proudest moment of his managerial career. He went to work on his coaching badges after retiring and, 12 months after taking charge of Derby, he achieved his ultimate goal in double-quick time: managing Chelsea. A lot has happened since, including a stint “babysitting” the Blues when put in interim charge in April 2023. That seven-week period was his last exposure to the top flight as a manager but the familiar voices of his assistants Joe Edwards and Chris Jones remain. After 20 months in charge, he is comfortably the longest-serving of the three English managers in the division (Michael Carrick, eight months; Gary O’Neil, three months). Fresh from being named the League Managers Association manager of the year, an award presented to him by Thomas Tuchel, this summer Lampard signed fresh terms until 2029.

Star signing

Never fall in love with a loan player? Coventry did not just score goals last season, they kept them out, too, Rushworth claiming the Championship golden glove for 17 clean sheets. An ever-present in the league, his performances earned him three end-of-season club awards. On Coventry’s open-top bus parade, Rushworth, handed a pen by the captain, Matt Grimes, signed a placard that read “Sign here Carl” in block capitals. Then, this month, he signed a real contract to join permanently from Brighton, who inserted a buyback clause. “He was this close to getting kicked out of the group chat,” the defender Jake Bidwell joked after embracing Rushworth on his return. Before his season at Coventry, he had enjoyed loans across the league pyramid with Walsall, Lincoln, Swansea and Hull, but now the highly-regarded 25-year-old will test himself at the highest level.

View image in fullscreen Coventry valued Carl Rushworth so highly they spent a club-record £22.5m to sign him permanently from Brighton. Photograph: Richard Hammersley/Shutterstock

Stat attack

Arsenal were not the only champions to make good use of dead-ball situations last season. Coventry led the Championship for set-piece goals, with 29. Only Bayern Munich (0.65 goals per game) bettered their average (0.63) in the top divisions in England, France, Germany, Italy and Spain. The issue is whether they will win enough corners and free-kicks in the Premier League to exploit this ability.

Set for a breakthrough

Promotion makes the jump from the academy to the first team that little bit bigger but Kai Andrews has at least made a dent in the senior squad. The 20-year-old, who made his debut aged 17, made seven substitute appearances last season before being loaned to Hibernian. Competition has only got fiercer since but Andrews has plenty of admirers. “There’s just something more about this kid; he has a presence – and that excites me,” said Craig Bellamy, who played for Coventry at the beginning of his career and handed an 18-year-old Andrews a shock call-up to the Wales squad approaching 18 months ago.

World Cup impact

Did Yirenkyi have an inkling that he would soon call Brandon Thomas-Asante a clubmate after the striker set him up to score his first World Cup goal for Ghana? Thomas-Asante, one of five players to reach double figures for Coventry last season, made inroads down the left flank and then squared the ball to the six-yard box, where Yirenkyi was on hand to strike a 95th-minute winner against Panama in their opener in Toronto. Haji Wright, Coventry’s top scorer last season, made two late substitute appearances for the USA, while Aurèle Amenda was part of the Switzerland squad that reached the last 16 but did not play a minute.

Sports.title: Atlético Madrid agree £34.1m deal for Tottenham’s Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Tottenham have reached an agreement with Atlético Madrid over the sale of their captain, Cristian Romero. Romero was given the green light by the club and Roberto De Zerbi to depart Spurs this summer after a turbulent 2025-26 campaign in which he served four separate suspensions.

Inter initially led the chase for the Argentina centre-back, but after talks with Spurs stalled, long-term admirers Atlético swooped in and a package of €40m (£34.1m) is set to secure Diego Simeone his target.

It will bring a rollercoaster five-year spell in north London to an end for Romero, who joined in 2021 and enjoyed mixed success under Antonio Conte before a strong bond was formed with Ange Postecoglou.

Romero wore the captain’s armband when Tottenham ended a 17-year trophy drought with victory over Manchester United in the 2025 Europa League final and produced a fine performance to ensure Postecoglou’s promise of silverware in his second season came true.

However, Postecoglou’s dismissal weeks later was met with a thinly veiled social media post in the direction of Spurs’ hierarchy by Romero and more followed during a chaotic last season where only a final-day win against Everton avoided relegation.

Romero, who was made captain by Thomas Frank ahead of the 2025-26 campaign, was in Argentina days before Tottenham’s 1-0 success over Everton to receive treatment on a knee injury before he got a flight back to be present in the stands. The return of Romero for the relegation decider only occurred after widespread criticism from Spurs supporters and it proved the final nail in the coffin for many fans.

The World Cup winner will exit Spurs after 156 appearances and link up with his compatriot Simeone, who has repeatedly talked up the quality of the Argentinian in recent seasons and will finally get his man this summer.

Tottenham have inserted a 15% sell-on clause in the deal and this imminent departure continues a summer of mass changes with De Zerbi overseeing a huge revamp of a squad which has finished 17th in consecutive seasons.

Newly promoted Hull have broken their transfer record to sign the Senegal defender Nobel Mendy from Spanish side Rayo Vallecano. They also signed Australia international Lucas Herrington on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Lucas Herrington became Australia’s youngest player to make a World Cup appearance this summer. Photograph: Alex Livesey/Fifa/Getty Images

The Tigers have not disclosed the fee for the 21-year-old Mendy but it exceeds the reported £20m they paid for the Greece goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis last week. Mendy, who has one international cap and previously played for Paris FC and Real Betis, has signed a five-year deal, with an option for a further 12 months. He finished his only season with Rayo Vallecano with an appearance in May’s Conference League final loss to Crystal Palace.

“I have wanted to play in the Premier League since I was little, so it’s a great challenge to face and I am ready for it,” Mendy told Hull’s website.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Herrington, 18, became Australia’s youngest player to start a World Cup game for the Socceroos this summer, and arrived from MLS side Colorado Rapids on a five-year deal.

Crystal Palace have re-signed Aston Villa’s Evann Guessand on loan for the season with an option to buy. The Côte d’Ivoire international made 14 appearances after moving to Selhurst Park in January until the end of last season, but in July Palace opted against making the move permanent.

The 25-year-old joined Villa from Ligue 1 side Nice for £30m last summer but failed to win a regular place in Unai Emery’s side.

Celtic have signed the Egypt winger Haissem Hassan from Spanish club Real Oviedo, subject to international clearance. The 24-year-old, who impressed at this summer’s World Cup, joins the Scottish champions on a four-year deal, with the option of a further 12 months.

“When I heard about Celtic being interested in me, I had to get here and be part of the club,” Hassan told the club’s website. Manager Martin O’Neill said Celtic had done “really well” to secure a player of Hassan’s quality amid interest from other clubs.

“He is someone who I think has the ability and experience to do very well for us, performing at a high level in domestic and international football,” said O’Neill.

Sports.title: Anderson still pained by England defeat but ready to shine at Manchester City
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson has admitted ­England’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina still pains him, but is hoping to use the confidence from his performances at the ­tournament to inspire the start of his Manchester City career.

Anderson will probably make his debut when City play ­the Premier League winners, Arsenal, on ­Sunday at the Principality ­Stadium in ­Cardiff for the Community Shield.

“It’s really hard,” Anderson said of England’s loss. “I’m still sort of ­struggling with that. There are highs and lows in football. It’s about how you bounce back.

“I’ve had three weeks to reflect on it, but now is a new season, you have to move forward.

I take huge confidence knowing I can perform on a World Cup stage. I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. That was a really good test for me.”

The 23-year-old is likely to become a significant figure in City midfield because of Barcelona’s interest in signing Rodri. A new £51m bid was made by the La Liga side on Wednesday, as they try to seal a deal for the 30-year-old. If the Ballon d’Or ­winner does depart, City’s new No 5 will be expected to be part of the plan to replace him in the middle of the park. Asked if he is similar in style to the Spaniard, Anderson said: “I think so. I can do various things within ­midfield and I’ll see where I get used.

“I’ll play anywhere. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that.”

Anderson joined from Nottingham Forest for what was briefly a record £116m fee [Morgan Rogers’s £117m move to Chelsea soon eclipsed it] for a British player – City had a ­longstanding interest in him while Pep Guardiola was in charge. Due to his extended World Cup exertions with England, the former ­Newcastle midfielder is yet to feature for City under their new head coach, Enzo Maresca.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Guardiola’s departure, though, did not made him debate his decision. “It’s such a huge club and the players they have are the best. I want to be surrounded by these sorts of ­players, proving myself on a daily basis.

“[Kevin] De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.”

Sports.title: Manchester United enjoy trip to Dublin with penalty shootout win over Leeds
Sports.content:
With blazing sunshine fading over a hot Dublin day, this penultimate friendly for Manchester United and Leeds United felt like a pre-season game on a far continent, not one staged a few hundred miles from the teams’ home across the Irish Sea.

The phoney-war element is always present whatever the locale, as ­players sharpen technique and fitness, so when Joshua Zirkzee’s instant left-foot shot met Diogo Dalot’s zipped-in cross and James Trafford saved low, all involved could be satisfied.

Even better for Michael Carrick’s men ensued: Bryan Mbeumo raced along the left and served the ball to Zirkzee who, again, hit a first-time effort that this time beat Trafford to his right.

Leeds had been scythed open, their right-side defenders, Jayden Bogle and Sebastiaan Bornauw, rendered awol by a lightning attack straight from the Carrick-Steve Holland ­training ground playbook.

Daniel Farke’s switch to a 3-5-2 at half-time of November’s 3-2 loss at Manchester City is credited, rightly, with saving their top-flight status, and the manager’s job.

Yet it can cause a retroactive-mode if the wingbacks retreat into a five-man rearguard. After Bogle and Rhys Chadwick did so, Mbeumo’s attempt, after one more United foray, underlined the problem.

More proactive, then, were two Ao Tanaka throw-ins that dipped into the area and posed those in red to scramble. When Leeds came straight back at them, a Tyler Fletcher shimmy backfired, and they profited.

The midfielder was robbed by Dan James who flipped the ball into the area where Brenden Aaronson stroked past Senne Lammens, who was helpless. So, too, Trafford when a Mbeumo rocket beat him, the bar saving Leeds, as, along the touchline, replacements prepared to enter for the second period.

Quick Guide Lewis-Skelly scores in Arsenal friendly as transfer speculation continues Show Myles Lewis-Skelly appeared to underline his commitment to Arsenal by setting aside transfer speculation to score in Wednesday’s 1-1 friendly draw with the Italian club Como. The 19-year-old has been linked with Chelsea and Manchester United amid uncertainty over his future. Starting in midfield, he capitalised on an error from the Como goalkeeper, Jean Butez, to put the hosts ahead in the 33rd minute at Emirates Stadium. Lewis-Skelly then made a heart sign to the crowd as he celebrated before tapping the club badge on his shirt on his way back to the centre circle. The England international signed a five-year contract with Arsenal last summer but his long-term future has come under scrutiny since he fell behind Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapié last term to become Mikel Arteta’s third choice left-back. While he started only five Premier League games across the course of the campaign, he enjoyed an end-of-season resurgence in centre midfield. Arsenal, however, are well-stocked in that position after signing Bruno Guimarães to join Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard and the World Cup winners Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Guimarães, who joined from Newcastle in a £75m deal, was introduced at half-time against Como to make his debut, while Lewis-Skelly was replaced in the 62nd minute by Merino. The Premier League champions were pegged back by Champions League-bound Como, who are managed by the former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, when Martin Baturina equalised in the 43rd minute. But Arsenal won the penalty shootout 4-3, with Guimarães and his fellow summer signing Christos Tzolis on target. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Before the game, Carrick had issued an update on those not involved. “Marcus [Rashford], Licha [Martínez] and Kobbie [Mainoo] aren’t quite ready yet,” he said. “We’re ­preserving them for this weekend [against Milan in Wroclaw].”

Missing, too, were Mason Mount, as a precaution, Tom Heaton, whose problem is being assessed and Harry Maguire, who joined training on Wednesday.

“Tonight is going to be ­historical,” screeched the enthusiastic PA announcer when billing this ­inaugural meeting between two ­English clubs at the cavernous stadium.

View image in fullscreen Brenden Aaronson slots home Leeds’s first-half equaliser. Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty Images

But Carrick’s three half-time changes were hardly stellar names to please the capacity crowd. Off went Patrick Dorgu, Andrey Santos and Mbeumo for the fringe players, Toby Collyer, Daniel Armer, an 18-year-old debutant, and Tynan Thompson, given a first outing since joining recently.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Farke’s changes ran to 10, with only Bornauw surviving, so now the question was how disjointed the contest might be. Encouragingly, Harry ­Wilson and Alfie Cresswell tested Lammens, then slick Zirkzee footwork took him in on goal.

But further disruption followed when Carrick made six more changes, including the introduction of his captain, Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans, his new £35m midfielder, and Matheus Cunha, who spearheaded the 4-2-3-1.

The result: a long lull before ­Lammens repelled a James Justin rasper, a Fernandes strike was ruled offside and the same player clipped the bar before penalties, to decide the Boyle Sports Cup, arrived.

Before the final whistle five fans rushed on for selfies with Fernandes and Tielemans – youngsters, sure, but a concerning security breach, ­especially as a sixth followed.

View image in fullscreen A capacity crowd of more than 80,000 turned up at Croke Park. Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty Images

United won the shootout 5-4, Noussair Mazraoui netting the decisive kick, and the teams wandered away offering scant clue how their 2026-27 season will be.

The pre-season results of United now read this victory, 1–1 against Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, 2–1 (Atlético Madrid), 5–0 (Rosenborg) and the 1–0 loss to Wrexham on 18 July. After this defeat, Leeds’s record is 2-0, against RB Leipzig, 4-2 (Liverpool), 1-0 win (Sunderland), and the 3-2 defeat, also to Wrexham, on 26 July.

Leeds finish their preparation by hosting Augsburg, while United make the trip to Poland. Last term they ended third, 24 points ahead of Leeds in 14th. Given the former’s thus far underwhelming transfer window – only Tielemans and Santos as major signings – they would take the same finish, as would Leeds, surely, as survival will be their priority.

Sports.title: Xavi Hernández appointed head coach of the Netherlands on four-year contract
Sports.content:
The former Barcelona head coach Xavi Hernández has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands. The 46-year-old Spaniard has agreed a contract to lead the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

He replaces Ronald Koeman, who stepped down following the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup.

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi won the World Cup as a player with Spain in 2010 and also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and 2012. He guided Barça to the La Liga title in 2023 after beginning his managerial career with Qatari club Al Sadd.

“I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team,” he said in a statement released by the Dutch Football Association (KNVB).

“As someone who received his training at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say that I am a bit of a son of Dutch football.”

Xavi’s appointment marks his first return to management since leaving Barcelona in 2024. He took over the Catalan club in November 2021, also succeeding Koeman, after making 767 appearances for the club.

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that also appeals to me enormously: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion, and conviction,” he said. “Of course, the most important goal is and always will be to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy. The potential for this is there, as well as a solid foundation to build upon.”

Former Liverpool head coach Arne Slot walked away from talks about replacing Koeman after saying he wants to remain in club football. His link to the role did not get beyond an initial approach.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“At this stage in my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day, something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team,” Slot told Voetbal International. “And [it is] why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.

“I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB [Dutch Football Association] and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week. For now, I believe club football still has a lot to offer me.”

Sports.title: Championship angst: why the sense of rejuvenation in EFL is not universal
Sports.content:
A new season is supposed to be about renewed hope and optimism, a fresh campaign opening up a world of possibilities, a clean slate. But with the English Football League due to kick off on Friday night when Wolves host Blackburn in the Championship, the sense of rejuvenation is not universal.

The lineup of Championship teams this season is fearsome. Wolves and West Ham, hitherto established Premier League clubs, have dropped into the second tier. Others such as Burnley, Middlesbrough and Southampton anticipate a promotion push. So perhaps supporters of those who are not enjoying parachute payment riches and squads still packed with top-flight talent are wise to feel cautious. Some fear a long slog of a season to come.

Blackburn fans, for example, saw their side scrape to the safety of a 20th-place finish last season, therefore would be forgiven for tempering their expectations before the trip to Molineux. Tony Mowbray has been brought back to Ewood Park as an experienced guiding hand, but the 62-year-old has a huge task to avoid a relegation battle.

Fans believe the Rovers owners and the club’s head of football operations, Rudy Gestede, have sold Mowbray short on players heading into the season, particularly in midfield. The 34-year-old Sam Morsy – described by Mowbray as “a real man, a soldier” – has added steel to that area of the pitch with his free transfer, but after Moussa Baradji and Jayden Fevrier he is only the third addition at Blackburn this summer. Mowbray wants and needs more.

“I’m a bit greedy for good players,” he said. “I keep saying to Rudy: ‘I just want good players, doesn’t really matter where they come from, what age they are.’ I want to see personality on the pitch, players who are desperate to win.”

Blackburn edged past Burton 2-1 in the Carabao Cup first round last week, though they required late goals from Andri Gudjohnsen and Fevrier, who Mowbray believes can bring “magic” on the right wing after signing from Stockport.

View image in fullscreen Bolton Wanderers celebrated victory in the League One playoff final but a tricky season lies ahead. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Down the road, there are two other Championship clubs feeling a similar sense of trepidation before the new campaign, and they meet at the Toughsheet Stadium on Saturday lunchtime, a game that could set the tone for their seasons. Bolton should still be on cloud nine; they finished last season with a 4-1 demolition of Stockport in the League One playoff final. Yet as the football world has witnessed this summer at York – where the manager, Stuart Maynard, was sacked and replaced by Scott Lindsey, despite winning the National League with 108 points – the afterglow of promotion can be short-lived. Reality bites quick.

And such is the chasm between the second and third tiers nowadays, the need for Steven Schumacher’s side to strengthen fast became paramount after that glorious day at Wembley. David Watson, Ben Davies, Akin Famewo, Luca Stephenson, Kyliane Dong and Gaizka Larrazabal have all arrived, but there is a feeling among the fanbase that a marquee addition is needed, especially in attack where they risk asking too much of the striker Sam Dalby. Schumacher’s admission last week that Bolton “can’t afford to waste money” rang alarm bells with the fanbase. There is not an embarrassment of riches in the pot but forward players must be signed.

“We know we’re short, especially at the top end of the pitch,” Schumacher said. “Our budget isn’t massive so we need to make sure we get the right players in, rather than just signing anybody to fill numbers. We need to try and consolidate this year, rebuild, get some more finances behind us, bring in a better squad that can keep us at this level, and then kick on.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Schumacher said that “this part of the journey is an exciting one” but it seems negativity among some fans has kicked in before a Championship ball has been kicked. A 1-0 defeat against Sheffield Wednesday in the Carabao Cup reinforced concerns around goalscoring, or the lack of it. Max Dean of Gent is coveted, but the striker is just 22 and his English football experience is limited to a short spell at MK Dons.

Preston will hope to take advantage of the uncertainty around Bolton on Saturday, but Paul Heckingbottom has endured his own problems in the transfer market this summer. A public spat with Ben Whiteman over the midfielder’s desire to join Wrexham left a cloud hanging above the club and saw the Lilywhites lose their club captain. Heckingbottom said Whiteman “crossed a line” and was frustrated by the saga.

Money has been spent at Deepdale this summer with Alfie Devine brought in from Tottenham for a fee in the region of £6m, while Callum Lang “feels like a new signing” according to Heckingbottom, having arrived in January for around £2m before getting injured. So the pressure is on Heckingbottom perhaps like never before. A run of just four wins from their final 20 matches of last season prompted a few fan murmurs of discontent towards the manager. With Preston almost investing £1.5m to install a modern hybrid pitch at Deepdale, the club expect better than last season’s 14th-place finish, but expectations can weigh heavy.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father.

Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

In a tribute on Instagram on Wednesday, Messi wrote: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you. I don’t know how ​to move forward. I only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I’m going to keep doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the tournament, where Argentina were beaten in the final by Spain, before rejoining his club side, Inter Miami, making his Major League Soccer return against Columbus at the start of this month.

Jorge had been a constant presence during his son’s career from his earliest days at Barcelona, with the World Cup the first time he had been absent from a major tournament. Messi revealed that his father, despite his deteriorating condition, had urged him to play for La Albiceleste in their ultimately unsuccessful attempt to defend their title.

“You always asked me to play in the last World Cup and a few days before it started was when you got worse,” he wrote. “It was the first time you weren’t going to be at a tournament … Every time a match ended, I would ‌wait and hope for your message. That’s when I realised how real the situation was.”

After tearfully celebrating the opening goal of his hat-trick against Algeria in the group stage, Messi had explained he was going through “a few difficult, complicated days” because of “something unrelated to football”. he said he ran out of energy in final.

“My legs couldn’t go on any more,” he wrote. “This time I tried to push myself beyond my ​physical limits, but I couldn’t. ​I never felt well … We weren’t champions, ​but you don’t know how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were ​right: I had to ‌be there and play ​it.”

Messi has earned 207 caps for Argentina since making his debut for his country in August 2005. He captained the side to World Cup glory in 2022, matching the achievement of Diego Maradona in 1986, though like Maradona he fell at the final hurdle when attempting to win back-to-back titles.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Messi did, though, break the record for total World Cup goals, with his strike against Egypt in the last 16 his 21st at the tournament and his 125th in all for Argentina. His World Cup tally was later surpassed by France’s Kylian Mbappé in the third-place playoff.

With his future uncertain it remains to be seen whether he will add to his remarkable CV of honours, which includes 10 La Liga titles, four Champions Leagues and eight Ballons d’Or in addition to that World Cup triumph in Qatar.

But he promised to honour his father’s memory through his own children: “I’m going to miss you so much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I will teach them and raise them the way you raised me.”

Sports.title: How Man City will replace Rodri - and the inconvenient truth for World Cup hero that shows they might be better off without him
Sports.content:
How Man City will replace Rodri - and the inconvenient truth for World Cup hero that shows they might be better off without him

Unlock more from Jack Gaughan inside the Man City camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Rodri is due in Manchester on Friday, after his planned back surgery following World Cup glory meant he was given two extra days' holiday. But in the context of that rehabilitation and the harsh reality that his future now lies away from Manchester City, it wouldn’t represent a great surprise if the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner did not return to the building for regular pre-season testing.

City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for a central midfielder in the final year of his contract, who was awarded player of the tournament last month. Somebody who often looked physically shot last season, yet was imperious at international level.

There is a balance to strike for director of football Hugo Viana in making sure City maximise Rodri's value while also realising that this orchestrated exit – heavily signposted for a year and solidified by Pep’s Guardiola goodbye, with the 30-year-old starting only 18 Premier League games in the last two seasons – likely only ends one way.

Guardiola called it last autumn, that City would not see the best of his metronome all season and that recaptured form would be reserved for the World Cup. The suggestion felt intriguing at the time, more by the way in which it was delivered – a little knowing, somewhat resigned. City’s medical staff were attempting to curb Rodri’s desire to to rush various injury comebacks.

There are those who believe his performances Stateside, when temperatures dictated that games were played at a slower pace, prove that there is still nobody better across Europe than him. But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts.

In the Premier League, the win ratio is exactly half with him starting. Without, it is 60.3 per cent. A very similar story plays out from 29 starts in all competitions. Never before in Rodri’s City career have the team won more games in his absence.

Manchester City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for Rodri, who was awarded World Cup player of the tournament last month

But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts

Although not an exact science – City still always concede fewer goals when he’s the deep midfielder – and a small sample size, it does represent a comparison worthy of note.

City, and Enzo Maresca, would prefer to plough on with him, of course. Their movements in the transfer window paint a picture of how this is only heading one way.

Proactive and forceful club denials around interest in Chelsea’s £120million-rated Enzo Fernandez at the beginning of the summer have now given way to silence. Fernandez wants to reunite with his old boss Maresca and those close to him believe the feeling to be mutual. Ayyoub Bouaddi, the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million.

City sources say Bouaddi's arrival is not linked to Rodri’s future and that they are pursuing him regardless of what happens, in a window that is threatening to become busy if Tijjani Reijnders and potentially another midfielder leave.

Yet his displays across almost 100 senior games, earning rave reviews for a physicality off the ball and intelligence on it, dictate that he can be ready to impact City’s fortunes. His minutes will have to be carefully monitored and managed.

What seemed apparent on Wednesday, when Elliot Anderson was unveiled to supporters during an event at the Etihad, was that the £116million club-record signing fancies more of a roaming ‘box-to-box’ role than filling Rodri’s void.

‘I’ve spoken to the manager a few times – he explained the sort of things that I need to do,’ said Anderson. ‘There is a lot of running, a lot of energy. It’s to try and control games. That is what I can do.

‘I’ll see where I get used. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that. Kevin De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi (right), the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million

There is a feeling that Enzo Fernandez (left) wants to reunite with Enzo Maresca, but for now Elliot Anderson (right) is the man City have identified as the one to run their midfield

City identified Anderson's aggression and punch in the pass as ideal for the way the Premier League operates these days. Maresca has operated with a two-man midfield in his pre-season fixtures – Mateo Kovacic and Reijnders against Atletico Madrid in South Korea on Sunday – and in that system, Anderson would appear as the one who springs forward, chipping in with the sort of goal he scored away at City during a 2-2 draw in March, arriving late.

Kovacic is ahead of Nico Gonzalez in the pecking order and expected to start Sunday’s Community Shield against Arsenal in Cardiff. Both Gonzalez and Kovacic have publicly declared that they do not wish to leave this summer.

The physical demands Maresca places upon his midfielders is huge, with Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki vying for the role pushed up alongside Erling Haaland. Maresca is looking at around half a dozen options as part of the two, with that second runner crucial. The way Reijnders crashed the boxes during their friendlies showcased exactly what is being preached on the training pitch.

‘I’ve taken take huge confidence knowing that I can perform on a World Cup stage,’ Anderson said, also admitting that he’s still struggling with England's semi-final defeat by Argentina. ‘Obviously I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. I had a big decision to make on who to join and I’m confident I’ve made the right one.’

Sports.title: LIV Golf's demise takes another blow as embattled tour tells players $40m season finale is CANCELED... despite still pushing ticket sales
Sports.content:
LIV Golf's demise takes another blow as embattled tour tells players $40m season finale is CANCELED... despite still pushing ticket sales

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

After weeks of speculation, LIV Golf has officially informed its players that the season finale in Michigan has been canceled. It appears, however, this has not been relayed to the ticket sales department.

Reports at the end of July hinted that the LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship was set to be scrapped, denying the 13 teams playing on the rebel circuit the chance to compete for the $40million prize.

According to The Telegraph, that decision is now official as players have been told the event is now off.

While an official announcement has not yet taken place, the outlet reports that Fox has removed the tournament from its TV listing and no infrastructure had been built at the course set to hold the event: The Cardinal at Saint John's.

This means that next week's tournament, LIV Golf Indiana, will be the final event of the 2026 season for LIV Golf after the Saudi Public Investment Fund announced it would no longer be funding the rebel circuit after this season's conclusion.

Despite the information being relayed to the players, emails from LIV Golf continued to advertise ticket sales for the Michigan event.

James Corrigan of The Telegraph posted a screenshot of said promotional email with the subject line 'Get your tickets for Aramco LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship 2026 - Grounds before they're gone!'

LIV Golf has informed its players that the $40m Team Championship has been canceled

However, it appears the rebel tour is continuing to advertise ticket sales to the Michigan event

The future of LIV remains uncertain after the Saudi PIF announced they were backing out

Comments underneath Corrigan's post claim LIV Golf doesn't show the Michigan event on their schedule anymore, however, users could still purchase tickets if they click on the link sent through the email.

It's yet another cancellation made in the wake of the PIF's pullout. Back in June, LIV Golf Louisiana was canceled.

This comes at a time where the future of the breakaway circuit continues to be shrouded in uncertainty.

Scott O'Neil, the chief executive of LIV, revealed last week that an investor had been lined up to fund the league's operations in 2027.

However, the identity of said investor has not been officially revealed and no agreements appear to have been signed.

Reports indicate that the deals hinge on keeping golf stars Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm in the roster.

The conclusion of the season now remains a mystery. It's not clear how the team race will be decided at the Indiana event, with players telling The Telegraph that they 'remain in the dark' on how a winner will be determined and whether the $40million in team prizes will be distributed.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick offers clear indication Marcus Rashford will STAY at Man United: Star in manager's plans as forward prepares for return to action against the man who exiled him
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford could make his first appearance since returning to Manchester United against AC Milan on Saturday – managed by Ruben Amorim, the man who bombed him out in the first place.

The England international has returned from a loan spell at Barcelona and is now intent on fighting to regain his place at Old Trafford.

He has been told he’s in Michael Carrick’s plans after United’s draw with Leeds in Dublin. By a quirk of fate, it is against Amorim’s Milan side that he will make his return, after an extended post-World Cup break.

Bryan Mbeumo led the line again here and got the assist for Joshua Zirkzee’s goal, but Carrick said of Rashford: ‘He’s our player. He’s come back great. He’s just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.’

The summer has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, with the results of the Mbeumo striker experiment yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroon international, 27, is far from your typical No9 but for Carrick, that is a big part of his appeal.

Marcus Rashford is in Michael Carrick's plans after his return to Manchester United

United want to give academy star Shea Lacey some space in the first team and he predominantly plays off the right. There is also Amad Diallo, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role. Then you must add in the fact United only have one orthodox No9 option, Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn’t kicked a ball during pre-season due to a shin injury – although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp. Rashford could nudge himself ahead of the Slovenian.

Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, especially if United do not sign another striker before the September 1 transfer deadline.

Mbeumo’s goals dried up in the second-half of last season and he struggled to rediscover the momentum that had United fans off their seats in the first-half of the campaign.

It led to questions over how Carrick could get the best out of him. But his double against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against Paris Saint-Germain and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Zirkzee to open the scoring here against Leeds in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo’s veins.

For the opening goal – and he should have had one of his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar – he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start.

Despite Carrick’s side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park. United won 5-4 on penalties.

Mbeumo is set to start as a centre forward at Hull City to kick-start United’s Premier League campaign on August 22. From there the sky feels like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

Sports.title: The encouraging signs emerging under Michael Carrick's coaching, Bryan Mbeumo passes latest No 9 audition - and the young star the club CANNOT afford to let go as Man United beat Leeds on penalties
Sports.content:
Manchester United edged out rivals Leeds United on penalties to win the pre-season Boyle Sports Cup inside a sold-out Croke Park.

While the shootout - which almost didn't happen due to a deluge of young pitch invaders at full-time - ultimately separated the sides, both managers will have taken plenty from this pulsating clash under the lights in Dublin.

Bryan Mbeumo's audition to be Manchester United's starting striker for the opening game of the season was strengthened with another smart display, while Brenden Aaronson finished off a brilliant move to level things up at 1-1 in the first half.

James Justin's costly penalty miss as the fifth taker for Leeds allowed Noussair Mazraoui to win it with the final act as Michael Carrick's side clinched the game 5-4 on spot-kicks.

Daily Mail Sport brings you some of the biggest talking points from an historic night in Dublin…

Joshua Zirkzee (left) and Bryan Mbeumo (right) starred as Manchester United took on Leeds

TRUST COACH CARRICK

One of the things that Ruben Amorim called for was time on the training pitch to imprint his ideas on the United squad.

They fluffed the Europe league final to secure a season without European football and bar a couple of encouraging flashes, tangible signs of style and progress never materialised.

So to see Manchester United playing as well as they have throughout this pre-season - yes, it's pre-season - is a sign of just what good training ground coaches Carrick and his staff are proving to be.

It's a collective effort between Carrick, Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans, Travis Binnion, and many analysts in the background.

Here against Leeds United, much as it was against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg last weekend, you can see tangible signs of progress in the way Carrick wants this team to evolve in its pressing and its play-style.

'He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways,' summer signing Youri Tielemans explained on Tuesday.

'It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht, you know. So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together.'

United are proving a lot more aggressive in the press and the defensive work of Andrey Santos in midfield, one of the summer signings to the tune of £50million, is pivotal.

The encouraging thing is that while these haven't been perfect performances either, there are more first team stars to come back in.

United lit up Croke Park from the start without captain and talisman Bruno Fernandes, without Tielemans, without Matheus Cunha, without the returning Marcus Rashford, without Benjamin Sesko, and Matthijs de Ligt, and Harry Maguire.

The way Leeds picked United off, capitalising on loose control from Tyler Fletcher, shows that there is still work to do.

But stylistically United, visibly at least, appear to be getting better by the game. For Manchester United fans, that's an incredibly encouraging sign.

Throughout pre-season you can see exactly what Michael Carrick is trying to implement

MBEUMO ON A HEATER

In a summer at Manchester United which has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, the results of the Bryan Mbeumo striker experiment are yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroonian is far from a typical No 9 but for Michael Carrick and Manchester United's staff, that is a big part of his appeal.

There are a multitude of factors at play here. United want to platform academy star Shea Lacey for a full-time first team role and he predominantly plays off the right. There's also Amad, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role.

And then you add in that United only have one orthodox No 9 option in Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn't kicked a ball during pre-season due to an ongoing shin injury, although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp.

So Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, should United not go and add another forward between now and the transfer deadline.

Mbeumo is going to start the season up top, that now looks clear, but expect Carrick to call upon Marcus Rashford, too.

'He's our player,' he said last night. 'He's come back great. He's just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.'

Mbeumo hit a real lull in front of goal in the second half of last season and struggled to rediscover momentum that had fans off their seats in the first half leading to question marks about how Carrick may get the best out of him.

But a brace against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against PSG, and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Joshua Zirkzee to open the scoring here in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo's veins right now.

For the opening goal here - and he should have had his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar - he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No 1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start. Despite Carrick's side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park.

Mbeumo is set to start as centre forward against Hull City to kickstart the Premier League campaign and from there the sky really does feel like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

TYNAN TIME

While he didn't quite get the loudest cheer of the night - that was reserved for the introduction of Bruno Fernandes off the bench - this was a huge milestone in the career of Tynan Thompson.

The 18-year-old arrived from Tottenham Hotspur this summer as an Emerging Talent Signing that Ineos and United's powers love, look at Ayden Heaven and numerous others.

This was Thompson's first taste of senior football at United and the first time he's been away and part of Carrick's group this pre-season.

Tynan Thompson got his first taste of senior football in a Manchester United shirt in Dublin

Thompson, who arrived in a deal that could eventually total £8m, got a pep talk from his manager moments before the second half restarted and the message, likely, was to be bold, be aggressive and have fun.

What we saw across 45 minutes was a player who looks unafraid to take people on and, in something of a quirk in the modern game, is a winger that likes to take people on on the outside.

A couple of times midway through the second half he managed to get down the left side with a quick burst and then drill a low cross in, only for Leeds to mop it up comfortably.

Sources at United won't pigeonhole Thompson as a first team player or an Under-21 player and he's likely to find himself straddling the two.

But don't underestimate the value of nights like these, in front of 82,000, with the likes of Fernandes and Cunha demanding the ball off you.

This isn't academy football any more…

HARRY'S STYLE

Speaking of rising stars, it should be an impossibility that Harry Amass is allowed to leave unless United go out and get another left back.

Sources have indicated that Amass has been told his best chance of regular minutes will come elsewhere and the club are unlikely to stand in his way for a loan or a permanent, if they get fair value.

That plan needs shelving immediately unless someone like Lewis Hall, who United have made two approaches for but failed on both occasions, walks through the door.

Amass may physically be on the smaller side in stature but he was dynamic in possession and fierce out of it here as Leeds looked to put him under real pressure, particularly early on before they clocked that they may be better off testing Diogo Dalot instead.

Amass has suitors aplenty should he walk out the door but with only Luke Shaw to call on as a bonafide left back right now, Amass should be staying until further notice.

There is no way Harry Amass can be allowed to leave without a new left back coming in

TRAFFORD IS TOP

One thing that Leeds do deserve credit for is the decisiveness they have shown in the goalkeeper department in getting a top talent in James Trafford.

They gave it as long as they could with Illan Meslier, then tried Lucas Perri out, and pivoted to Karl Darlow, now of Manchester United, before paying a club record £40m for him.

Officially Trafford got the Man of the Match here before it went to a penalty shootout and he did make a number of fine saves to keep Manchester United out, not least denying one effort from Zirkzee, and another from Mbeumo.

It cannot be understated just what a difference a truly top goalkeeper can make and if Leeds are to kick on like Brighton and Bournemouth did in getting into Europe, it is moves like Trafford that will go a long way to moving the needle.

MAKE IRELAND A YEARLY TRIP

Lastly, a sold out Croke Park was absolutely incredible, and a trip United should make yearly if the logistics were feasible.

The appetite for Manchester United in these parts is understandably huge and credit as well to the Leeds United contingent who travelled in good numbers.

Naturally the pre-season appeal is wherever the money is for Premier League clubs and the answer for Manchester United is often the United States.

But they could do a lot worse than secure themselves a near-enough home game in Ireland given how many fans turned out for this one.

A cracking trip that should give United's execs pause for thought.

Sports.title: Why the alarm bells should be ringing at Newcastle after defeat by Everton: Squad's lack of depth exposed, the key man who looks out of sorts and midfield puzzle new boss Matthias Jaissle must solve, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Why the alarm bells should be ringing at Newcastle after defeat by Everton: Squad's lack of depth exposed, the key man who looks out of sorts and midfield puzzle new boss Matthias Jaissle must solve, writes CRAIG HOPE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

In their new change kit, Newcastle United were the ‘shrinking violets’ during a 3-1 defeat by Everton at Murrayfield.

The loss raises serious questions over the squad’s readiness for the Premier League season, with new boss Matthias Jaissle having inherited a group lacking leadership as well as quality in key areas.

David Moyes’ side were the deserved winners after goals from Thierno Barry, Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George settled a contest in which the Toffees showed more control and composure. Harvey Barnes fired a late reply for the Magpies.

Here, our chief footballer reporter Craig Hope brings you his four big takeaways for Newcastle to consider…

NEW FACES NEEDED

This was not a ‘reality check’ for Newcastle, because the reality of their situation was already blindingly obvious. They have lost four of their best and most experienced players this summer and head coach Eddie Howe said he could not continue on the eve of pre-season.

Here, it was not just holes in Newcastle’s XI that were exposed, but the depth of their squad looks alarmingly shallow. They need two full-backs, better midfielders and a fresh spark in attack. The danger for Jaissle is that he makes a losing start because he has been left short.

New boss Matthias Jaissle has plenty to think about but the problems were not unexpected

We understand that Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba is among those the manager admires, and the club have him on their list of targets. It is not an active transfer – the 22-year-old currently has an ankle injury – but our sources say it is one to keep an eye on as the window progresses.

Baleba would be an ambitious move, but Newcastle need to be just that if they are to give their new boss a squad that is able to compete in the top-flight this term. For right now, you would forecast a season-long struggle at the wrong end of the table.

On transfers, Jaissle said: ‘I think you all see the matches. You're also smart enough to see the needs in the squad. We handle these things internally. We are aware of what we need. There's still some time.’

He added: ‘For sure, we cannot be on the peak (against Liverpool on the opening day). This is clear. We're just working now for a couple of days.’

SVEN LOOKS SHORT

Sven Botman signed a new four-year contract in January but his performances since have been below the level that earned him that deal. Insiders were concerned that he looked too rigid in his movement towards the end of the season, and that worry has extended into the summer.

The Dutch centre-back is a class act at his best, but he was again at fault for a goal here and his sloppiness on the ball perhaps betrays a lack of confidence. After a series of injuries, the wider concern would be that his best days are behind him. He has a lot to prove this season. For now, Dan Burn would appear a better bet at left-sided centre-back alongside Malick Thiaw.

Sven Botman looked a little off the pace at Murrayfield as Everton outclassed Newcastle

MIDFIELD RIDDLE

For five years under Howe, Newcastle have played with a midfield three. Jaissle, in his first two games, has started with a 4-2-3-1, and an absence of control was all too evident during the first-half period in which Everton scored twice.

Joelinton and new signing Aladji Bamba were the pair in the middle, but the former has always preferred the insurance of two team-mates alongside him, allowing him to charge around and impose his physical superiority.

He is not suited to a more disciplined role in which he needs to take better care of the ball, while Bamba, 20, clearly needs time before he is ready to start in the Premier League. The Frenchman, formerly of Monaco, has made only 25 senior appearances in his career.

If Newcastle going into the season opener against Liverpool with this midfield, you suspect it would not end well.

Harvey Barnes scored a consolation goal for the Geordies, giving their fans something to cheer

STEUR THE POSITIVE (AGAIN)

On a positive note, Jacob Ramsey and Sean Steur were a better combination in the second half. Steur, 18, has been Newcastle’s best player during pre-season and he again showed a maturity beyond his teenage years. His willingness to take the ball in tight areas – and then keep it – is exactly what this team needs in a world without Bruno Guimaraes.

Steur apart, however, ball retention is going to be a problem for Newcastle. And when they have a defence that looks short of pace, the opposition springing quick breaks on the back of turnovers should be a worry for Jaissle.

Sports.title: Arsenal's next top prospect shines in absence of key man, Myles Lewis-Skelly makes his case after doubts over his future - and why time is running out for Gabriel Jesus
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly struck in the first half in Arsenal’s 1-1 draw against Cesc Fabregas’ Como side amid speculation around his future.

Lewis-Skelly's effort was cancelled out by Martin Baturina two minutes before the break in what proved to be a real test for Mikel Arteta's men.

The Gunners went on to win 4-3 on penalties, thanks largely to David Raya. Arsenal are back in action when they face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport's ISAAN KHAN brings you the main talking points from their win over the Italian side.

Marli Salmon stands out

There’s another young gem coming through Arsenal’s Hale End pipeline: enter Marli Salmon.

He stepped up on a night where Mikel Arteta threw down the challenge to his youngsters.

Salmon and Max Dowman, both 16, started, as well as Theo Julienne, 18, who made his first senior team start.

Salmon in particular stood out, for the rarity of a 16-year-old starting in a first-team match at centre back.

The defender last season would typically come on at right back when substituted on in the odd first-team game — once in the Champions League and three times in the FA Cup (he started against Mansfield Town).

Marli Salmon was given a warm embrace from his manager Mikel Arteta when he came off

He coped well and wasn’t deterred by the physical challenge, playing with steel and conviction.

The opposition were wary of taking Salmon on, with the menacing Gabriel alongside him.

His runs and confidence on the ball made the real mark, as he progressed into the opposition half on occasion, evading players with a burst of speed. That takes guts and took the crowd by surprise.

What a baptism of fire such an experience is, and one he will no doubt remember.

Arteta’s confidence in the teenager saw Salmon stay on the pitch until the 88th minute.

He stepped up, alright.

Lewis-Skelly makes his point

A heart-shaped celebration and hands folded in a prayer motion, Myles Lewis-Skelly made his point.

The teenager struck in the first half amid reports suggesting the 19-year-old has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United by intermediaries, which Arsenal have insisted isn’t the case.

Though Lewis-Skelly brushed the noise aside to enjoy a promising display in a young line-up.

Goalkeeper Jean Butez’s clearance was headed down by Lewis-Skelly to Gabriel Martinelli, who teed up the teenager to strike home on 33 minutes.

The goal was met by chants of ‘Myles Lewis-Skelly, he’s one of our own’, on an evening he used to remind observers of his talents.

Myles Lewis-Skelly delivered a clear message with his celebration amid talk over his future

Yet, it was the midfielder’s actions after the goal which reflected where his intentions lie.

Lewis-Skelly clasped his hands together towards the crowd before making out a heart sign in a clear sign of intent.

He is a fine player, and one who started in last season’s Champions League final.

His ceiling is high — and his future is bright at Arsenal.

Little chance of resurrection for Jesus

The gauntlet had been laid. With Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz on the bench, Gabriel Jesus started as the No 9.
