World.title: Karnataka bandh: What will remain open? Which services will be affected?
World.content:
With various Kannada outfits calling for a Karnataka bandh on Thursday (August 13, 2026), more organisations and associations are expected to decide on extending their support by Wednesday (August 12) evening.

However, veteran Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj has said that they will definitely proceed with the bandh. As a precursor to the event, Mr. Nagaraj’s group has also called for a demonstration with “brooms” at Majestic Bus Stand on August 12.

The bandh, scheduled from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., is unlikely to affect public or private transport, shops and commercial establishments, hotels or eateries. Schools and offices are also expected to function as usual. Essential services such as healthcare, grocery stores, pharmacies and banks are expected to remain functional. Transport services are also likely to operate normally, as autorickshaw and cab unions have extended only moral support to the bandh.

While Mr. Nagaraj had initially said that the bandh in the State was in protest against the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) directive to release water to Tamil Nadu, he clarified on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that the bandh was also intended to highlight all major irrigation and development issues, including the Kalasa-Banduri and Mekedatu projects.

A clearer picture of which services are likely to be disrupted and which ones will function normally will emerge by August 12 evening, as hotel associations, cab and autorickshaw unions, and traders’ associations are expected to announce their decisions evening after meetings with their respective Union members.

Private schools to remain open

Meanwhile, private schools, including the Karnataka Associated Management of Schools (KAMS), have withdrawn their earlier advisory regarding the closure of schools in connection with the ‘Cauvery Bandh’, citing the loss of academic days.

At the same time, KAMS expressed its moral and peaceful support for the cause of protecting Karnataka’s legitimate interests in the Cauvery water dispute. “As a symbolic gesture of solidarity, school management representatives, teaching staff and non-teaching staff may wear a black ribbon or black strip on the day of the Bandh, without disrupting academic activities,” said D.Shashikumar, General Secretary, KAMS.

KAMS has also advised its member schools to use this occasion as an educational opportunity. It said that students from Classes 5 to 12 may be provided with age-appropriate and factual awareness about the history and background of the Cauvery water dispute, Karnataka’s dependence on Cauvery water for drinking, agriculture and livelihoods, the difficulties faced during years of deficit rainfall and water scarcity, as well as the reasons behind Karnataka’s concerns.

Symbolic protest

The Karnataka Kavalu Pade (KKP), which held a meeting in Mysuru with various Kannada outfits, students’ organisations, farmers’ leaders and progressive groups, has decided to indirectly support the bandh. Instead, KKP President Mohan Kumar Gowda said members of the outfit would stage a symbolic protest at Harding Circle, also known as Jayachamarajendra Circle, in the city.

“Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has said that farmers and Kannada activists can rest, since his government has promised to protect our interests. As the CM has given such an assurance, we will lie down for an hour at the Harding Circle, starting 11 a.m.,” Mr. Gowda said.

World.title: Morning Digest: Centre softens stance on FCRA Bill after minority groups appeal; Justice Varma’s withdrawal from probe cannot end statutory inquiry, says Lok Sabha panel, and more
World.content:
Centre softens stance on FCRA Bill following appeals by minority groups

The first indication of the Union Government’s softening of stance on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, emerged on August 9, when several Christian organisations launched coordinated appeals on YouTube, Facebook and WhatsApp, urging the Centre to either refer the Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) or withdraw it altogether. The appeals were seen as an attempt to provide the government with an honourable route to step back from pushing the legislation through Parliament.

Justice Varma’s withdrawal from probe cannot end statutory inquiry, says Lok Sabha panel

The three-member committee constituted to investigate the discovery of ‘burnt currency notes’ at the official residence of Justice Yashwant Varma has said that the former judge withdrew from the committee’s proceedings too late. The committee’s report, in a way, responds to questions in the public domain such as why it chose to continue its work and submit the report to Parliament even after Justice Varma ceased to be a judge with his resignation, with immediate effect, on April 9.

China says border with India ‘generally stable at the moment’

The India-China border is “generally stable at the moment”, China’s Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026), in response to queries about recent reports of rising tensions in Arunachal Pradesh’s eastern sector. When asked about these reports on Tuesday (August 11), India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in border areas was of “utmost importance”. He did not deny the reported rise in tensions since late July, in an area where both sides have been patrolling, with overlapping claims.

Kashmiri Pandit killings: J&K Police’s special cell reopens 1990 case; searches multiple locations

The Jammu and Kashmir Police’s special cell on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) carried out searches of terror suspects in the Union Territory (UT) and started reinvestigating a case of double murder of a Kashmiri Pandit father and son in 1990. Officials said multiple locations in south Kashmir’s Dooru in Anantnag district were raided to investigate the killing of Kashmiri Pandit writer Sarwanand Koul Premi and his son Virender Koul. According to the First Information Report (FIR), the bodies of the victims were found hanging from a tree in Kokernag, Anantnag, in 1990.

Former A&NI Chief Secretary said Shompen tribe must ‘adopt modern lifestyle’ brought by GNI project, alleges Tribal Council

Tribal leaders have accused the Andaman and Nicobar island administration of seeking to drag the Shompen, an isolated indigenous community into a “modern lifestyle” as part of the controversial Great Nicobar Island development project. The project includes a proposed power plant at Galathea, located near Shompen settlements.

India’s first ‘private, branded’ train to run as ‘Sprite’ Tejas Express

India’s first ‘private, branded’ train, launched by the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) between Lucknow and Delhi, will run as the ‘Sprite’ Tejas Express. After IRCTC awarded  rights through train branding of the Lucknow-Delhi-Lucknow Tejas Express to M/s Sprite for a period of six months, the North Eastern Railway was told that Train 82501/82502 Lucknow-Delhi-Lucknow IRCTC Tejas Express should be announced as the ‘Sprite’ Tejas Express from August 19, 2026 to November 11, 2026, sources in the Railways said.

Rape survivors don’t need court approval to terminate pregnancies up to 24 weeks: Madhya Pradesh High Court

Rape survivors, with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, do not require the permission from a court to seek a legal termination of pregnancy, the Madhya Pradesh High Court has said. A Single Bench of Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt in Indore on August 11 made the remarks hearing a petition filed by the father of a 16-year-old sexual assault survivor who sought the court’s approval for the girl’s 18-week pregnancy. The petition cited extreme mental trauma for the survivors to continue with the pregnancy.

Delhi High Court seeks clarity over Meta’s policy on access to Rights Manager

The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) sought clarity from Meta over its policy governing access to its Rights Manager tool, after concerns were raised that fraudulent actors have allegedly exploited the platform’s copyright-protection mechanism to target original content.

Seven dead, many injured in Mumbai landslip

At least seven people died, and several others were injured after a landslip struck Mumbai’s Ghatkopar area in the early hours of Wednesday (August 12, 2026) following heavy rains. Rescue operations are underway to trace one person believed to be trapped under debris. Mumbai’s civic body, Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), reported it as a Level-II incident — a serious incident requiring additional resources and coordination beyond the immediate ward — that occurred at 3:48 a.m. at Gaushiya Chawl in Chirag Nagar of Ghatkopar West. The soil and debris from the hillside collapsed onto two to three houses nearby, according to BMC Mayor Ritu Tawde, who visited the site to inspect operations.

Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who pushed reforms and India ties, dies of illness at 97

Zhu Rongji, the former Premier of China who played a key role in driving China’s economic reforms and transforming the country into a global economic power, died on Wednesday (August 12, 2026), aged 97. Zhu passed away in Beijing from illness, the State-run Xinhua news agency said, adding that an obituary issued by the ruling Communist Party “extolled Zhu as an excellent Party member, a time-tested and loyal communist fighter, and an outstanding proletarian revolutionist, statesman and leader of the Party and the State.”

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, youngest person to hold role, to leave at month’s end

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, the youngest person to hold the role, will leave at month’s end, U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Wednesday (August 12, 2026). Ms. Leavitt, 28, just recently returned to the White House after taking a brief leave for the birth of her second child in May. Ms. Leavitt has been one of the most visible advocates of Mr. Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement. The Republican president described her as one of his “most trusted aides” in a social media post announcing her departure.

Total darkness, then sunset as full eclipse wows spectators in Spain

Spectators across Spain watched in wonder, some whipping off their protective ‌glasses and rising to their feet in unison, as a rare total solar eclipse swept across the ​north of the country on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) evening, plunging it into darkness. Spain deployed a massive police contingent ⁠and set up special viewing spots across rural areas that offered the best views of the spectacle.

The marathoner technocrat who gave new direction to Tata Group

Natarajan Chandrasekaran, the chairman of Tata Sons, who announced his exit from the position at the end of his tenure in February next, will be known for giving new directions to the Tata Group and putting big bets on high technology-oriented businesses after taking over the reins in 2017.

SL vs IND Tests | India arrives in the Emerald Isle seeking a fresh path in Tests

The Indian Ocean lapsing into liquid sighs and roaring waves is entwined with Galle’s topography. This coastal town with a colonial past is leafy and charming. In this Sri Lankan amalgam of fine aesthetics and overwhelming history, India is seeking a fresh path in Tests. The two-Test series commencing with the first one here from Saturday (August 15, 2026) offers Shubman Gill’s men a rope to pull themselves up from the pit they sunk into in cricket’s longest format.

Sports Ministry pulls the plug on TTFI

The Sports Ministry on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) suspended the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) as the National Sports Federation for the sport with immediate effect, citing repeated non-compliance with government directions, governance deficiencies and concerns over athlete welfare and selection procedures.

World.title: Karnataka Bandh unlikely to disrupt normal life as most organisations extend only moral support
World.content:
Normal life is unlikely to be affected on Thursday (August 13) despite the bandh call given by Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj against the directive to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, as most organisations have extended only moral support to the call.

Karnataka bandh: What will remain open? Which services will be affected?

The bandh, scheduled from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., is unlikely to affect public or private transport, shops and commercial establishments, hotels or eateries. Schools and offices are also expected to function as usual. Essential services such as healthcare, grocery stores, pharmacies and banks are expected to remain functional. Transport services are also likely to operate normally, as autorickshaw and cab unions have extended only moral support to the bandh.

On Wednesday, Mr. Nagaraj said that the Kannada Okkoota had decided to go ahead with the bandh and that he would not call it off. He also said they would carry out a rally from Town Hall to Freedom Park at 11 a.m.

“From 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., the bandh will be effective. Mandya will be entirely shut down, and complete support will be received in Hubballi, Dharwad, Raichur and Ballari,” he said.

While Mr. Nagaraj had initially said that the bandh in the State was in protest against the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) directive to release water to Tamil Nadu, he clarified on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that the bandh was also intended to highlight all major irrigation and development issues, including the Kalasa-Banduri and Mekedatu projects.

As a precursor to the event, Mr. Nagaraj’s group held a demonstration with “brooms” at Majestic Bus Stand on August 12 before being escorted away by the police.

Meanwhile, Kannada outfit Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV), which has been at the forefront of several protests in the state, has said that it is not extending support to the bandh. Dinesh Kumar, organising secretary of KRV, said the bandh would not solve the issue, but a legal battle would, which the government was pursuing.

Rudramurthy of the Auto Rickshaw Drivers’ Union and Tanveer Pasha of OTU both told The Hindu said they were only extending moral support to the bandh, as stopping operations would disrupt the lives of lakhs of people.

Emphasising that they support the State’s lawful efforts to secure Karnataka’s rightful share of water for drinking and irrigation purposes, K. Radhakrishna Holla, president of the Karnataka State Travel Operators Association, said they were not extending support to the bandh, but only moral support to the cause.

“Our transport, tourism and service sectors are directly connected with the daily needs of the public. In an internationally recognised city like Bengaluru, continuity of transport, tourism, hospitality, business and other essential services is extremely important,” he said.

Educational institutions to remain open

Meanwhile, private schools, including those affiliated with the Karnataka Associated Management of Schools (KAMS), have withdrawn their earlier advisory regarding the closure of schools in connection with the ‘Cauvery Bandh’, citing the loss of academic days.

“As a symbolic gesture of solidarity, school management representatives, teaching staff and non-teaching staff may wear a black ribbon or black strip on the day of the bandh without disrupting academic activities,” said D. Shashikumar, general secretary, KAMS.

P.C. Rao of the Bruhat Bengaluru Hotels Association also said that the association was extending only moral support, citing food as an essential service.

Police warn against bandh

Bengaluru police have warned against forced shutdowns and road blockades. In a statement, the police said several organisations had called for the bandh, while others had informed the Bengaluru City Police that they were not supporting it. The police said citizens have the democratic and fundamental right to express their views and hold peaceful protests within the framework of the law. However, they stressed that the rights of those who do not wish to participate must also be respected.

“No individual or organisation should force, threaten or compel anyone to participate in the bandh,” the police said, warning against the forced closure of shops, establishments and institutions, obstruction of traffic, and compelling people to participate in protests against their will.

Precautionary security arrangements have been made across Bengaluru, with adequate police deployment, patrolling and security measures at important and sensitive locations.

World.title: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, youngest person to hold role, to leave at month’s end
World.content:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, the youngest person to hold the role, will leave at month’s end, U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

Karoline Leavitt, youngest White House press secretary, will make her debut in briefing room

Ms. Leavitt, 28, just recently returned to the White House after taking a brief leave for the birth of her second child in May.

From 2024: Trump names young Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary

Ms. Leavitt has been one of the most visible advocates of Mr. Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement. The Republican president described her as one of his “most trusted aides” in a social media post announcing her departure.

He said Ms. Leavitt “will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect! Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections.”

Ms. Leavitt recently returned to work after taking leave following the birth of her second child, a daughter, in May. She also has a two-year-old son.

“The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life,” Ms. Leavitt said in a social media post.

Mr. Trump did not outline plans for who might replace her in the high-profile role.

She worked as a spokesperson for MAGA Inc., a super PAC supporting Mr. Trump, before joining his 2024 campaign. In 2022, she ran for Congress in New Hampshire, winning a 10-way Republican primary before losing to incumbent Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas.

During Mr. Trump’s first term in office, Leavitt worked as a press aide in the White House press office. She then became communications director for New York Republican Rep. Elise Stefanik.

Ms. Leavitt briefed from the White House press room less frequently than some of her recent predecessors. Mr. Trump, who regularly engages with reporters during White House events and during his travels, primarily deployed Ms. Leavitt to Fox News and other conservative news outlets to trumpet his agenda and take shots at Democrats and the mainstream media.

Mr. Trump’s first-term press secretaries were Sean Spicer and Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who were known for quarrelling with reporters. Another, Stephanie Grisham, never held a briefing. Her successor, Kayleigh McEnany, often lectured the news media during her appearances in the press briefing room.

World.title: Mumbai biker on the way to Bastar killed in road accident
World.content:
A 24-year-old woman from Mumbai — en route to Chhattisgarh’s Bastar region as part of a bikers’ group – was killed after her vehicle was hit by another vehicle, suspected to be a truck, in Balod district early on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

The woman, Riddhi Divyesh Thakkar, 24, was a resident of Maharashtra’s Borivali (West), and part of a group of 20 bikers who had planned a tour from Raipur to Bastar.

Balod Superintendent of Police Kiran Chavan said that the incident occurred near Markatola Ghat, Thakkar was struck by an unidentified four-wheeled vehicle (possibly a truck), resulting in severe injuries and fractures to both her legs.

“Following a call to the ‘112’ emergency service, a vehicle from the Charama police station area transported her to the community health centre, Charama; she was subsequently referred to Shriram Hospital in Dhamtari, where she passed away during treatment. A post-mortem examination is currently being conducted at the District Hospital in Dhamtari. The incident site falls under the jurisdiction of the Purur police station, where the FIR will be registered,” said Mr. Chavan.

The errant driver or the vehicle had not been identified till Wednesday (August 12) evening. According to social media posts that were shared online, the group, which had bikers from different parts of Maharashtra, had left Raipur, having completed the earlier leg of their tour from Nagpur to Raipur a day earlier. It is learnt that the fellow bikers were returning home after the incident.

World.title: Cauvery water dispute hearing in Supreme Court posted to August 17 as Judge falls ill
World.content:
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) observed that the Cauvery water dispute between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka has been allocated to the Bench presided over by his colleague and next-in-line to be top judge as per the seniority norm, Justice Vikram Nath, who is down with viral fever.

The Chief Justice, heading a three-judge Bench of the Supreme Court, said Justice Nath would not be presiding over his Bench this week.

The case was initially expected to be listed on August 13 to hear a plea filed by the State of Tamil Nadu seeking a judicial direction to Karnataka to implement a Central Water Management Authority (CWMA) decision of July 30 to ensure the release of 3500 cusecs for 15 days from its two reservoirs at Kabini and Krishna Raja Sagara. Tamil Nadu has approached the Supreme Court for the release of 4.536 TMC (at the rate of 3500 cusecs for 15 days) on or before August 12.

Karnataka bandh: What will remain open? Which services will be affected?

However, on August 12, the Chief Justice said the case would now be posted on August 17 due to the unavailability of Justice Nath.

The oral observations from the CJI came during an oral mentioning made by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), represented by senior advocate P. Wilson, of a separate application filed by Tamil Nadu’s Opposition party in the Cauvery for the release of water essential to protect the water-starved agricultural lands in the State’s lower riparian districts.

The party had said this could be ensured by releasing about 7,000 cusecs of the river water on a per-day basis at Biligundlu for over a period of 15 days. It had asked the court to direct the CWMA to monitor the releases and to file a compliance report.

The application had submitted that despite the binding directions of the CWRC and CWMA, the State of Karnataka had “neither released the water nor evinced the slightest intention of doing so”.

“About 14.913 lakh acres (net area) in the Cauvery delta are dependent on the Mettur reservoir for irrigation, which in turn depends upon the flows realised at Biligundlu from the releases made by Karnataka from its reservoirs. About four million farmers and about 10 million agricultural labourers directly and indirectly depend on Mettur water for their very livelihood,” the application had said.

The party had submitted that farmers of the lower riparian districts of Tamil Nadu like Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Tiruchirappalli and other delta districts, were the worst affected by the non-release of water.

“The Kuruvai crop already raised is withering for want of water,” the application had said.

World.title: Bills for delimitation of Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporation passed in West Bengal Assembly
World.content:
The West Bengal Legislative Assembly on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) passed two bills paving the way for delimitation of wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation.

Also read | Firhad Hakim resigns as Kolkata Municipal Corporation Mayor

With the passage of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Howrah Municipal Corporation (Second Amendment) Bill, 2026 during special session of the Assembly the number of wards in Kolkata municipal area will increase from 144 to 209 and wards in the Howrah municipal area will increase from 50 to 68.

The population of Kolkata Municipal Corporation is estimated to be 6.7 million and Howrah Municipal Corporation is 1.6 million.

Speaking on the amendment bills, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the legislation passed by the Assembly only dealt with increasing the number of wards and that the actual delimitation would be undertaken subsequently by the State Election Commission (SEC). Mr. Adhikari also added that people will have an opportunity to air their grievances and there will be at least two all party meetings.

Former Kolkata Municipal Corporation Mayor Firhad Hakim said that he was not opposing the reorganisation and delimitation of the wards in principle but it should be made clear on what policy or criteria the entire process is being carried out. Mr. Hakim, who is a rebel Trinamool Congress MLA who has aligned with Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, has been one of the most prominent Muslim leaders of the State. “It should also be made clear whether the boundaries of the new wards are being altered by targeting any particular community,” Mr. Hakim said, raising questions on the political move behind the delimitation exercise and increasing the wards in Kolkata by 65 wards. Similar concerns were raised by another Kolkata MLA Javed Khan, who has also joined the rebel camp of Trinamool Congress led by Mr. Banerjee.

Minister for Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Agnimitra Paul, who introduced both the bills, defended the government’s decision to increase the number of wards, saying the move to increase the number of wards in the municipalities was aimed at improving civic services. “The previous governments did not do work for improving the civic facilities,” Ms. Paul told media persons. MLAs of the BJP who participated in the discussion raised questions about uneven distribution of voters in certain wards of Kolkata and Howrah.

The tabling and passage of the bills comes at a time when most of the civic bodies have turned defunct in the State. After the Bharatiya Janata Party came to power in West Bengal in May 2026, there has been mass resignation of councillors across the civic bodies. All the councillors of Kolkata Municipal Corporation have resigned, and the largest civic body of the State is being administered by a civil servant. The West Bengal government wants to complete the delimitation exercise before civic polls are held by the end of the year.

World.title: Student wounded, young suspect in custody after shooting at Georgia high school
World.content:
A shooting at a Georgia high school has left one student wounded, and a teenage suspect who fled was later taken into custody, police said.

The shooting at Warner Robins High School involving two ninth-graders occurred just one week into the new school year and prompted a response from dozens of law enforcement officers. Warner Robins is about 164 km southeast of Atlanta.

“Today a call that we train for every year happened to come to Houston County,” Sheriff Matt Moulton said at an evening news conference.

The injured student was taken to a hospital for treatment of non-life-threatening injuries. Mr. Moulton did not specify the type of injuries the student had.

It wasn't immediately known whether the school has metal detectors in place. Mr. Moulton declined to take questions at the news conference, citing the active investigation.

The sheriff said a group of students was inside a school bathroom when a verbal altercation between two students escalated into a physical fight. One student was shot at 2:15 p.m., and the suspect fled. A school resource officer arrived quickly, applied tourniquets to the student's injuries and remained until emergency services personnel arrived.

An hour later, the suspect was caught “without further incident” in a neighbourhood about 800 metres from the school, Mr. Moulton said.

“The school threat protocol and our training was followed perfectly today," Mr. Moulton said. "Fortunately what could have been a much-worse incident was minimised to us only having one student injured.” Houston County Schools Superintendent Richard Rogers said the school would be closed for students on Thursday (August 13, 2026) and Friday (August 14, 2026) and for staff on Thursday. Crisis counselors would be available at the school for staff on Friday and for students on Monday (August 17, 2026) .

“We're going to focus on healing,” Mr. Rogers said.

World.title: Taliban support fuels deadlier TTP attacks in Pakistan: UN
World.content:
• Taliban chief reportedly warned outfit to halt attacks or risk losing support

• UN report points to training links involving TTP, BLA, Al Qaeda

• ISIL-K attacks decline in Afghanistan, but increase in Pakistan

ISLAMABAD: The Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group, according to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report.

The report also points to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

The 38th report of the UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team, covering the period from Dec 16, 2025, to June 9, 2026, said that “cross-border attacks between Pakistan and Afghanistan escalated, provoked by a high number of attacks by Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakis­tan against Pakistan”.

Like previous editions, the report was unequivocal in its assessment of Kabul’s role, saying that “the de facto authorities (Taliban) continued their support to the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which escalated attacks against Pakistan, provoking military exchanges”.

It noted concern among member states that the continuing conflict could create opportunities for terrorist groups and generate additional security challenges for the region.

Taliban’s dual-track approach

The assessment nevertheless recorded some initial steps by the Taliban authorities to contain the TTP, although these appeared aimed more at managing the group than dismantling its infrastructure.

The report said Afghan authorities had relocated around 2,000 TTP fighters and their families from areas along the Pakistani border to deeper inside Afghanistan in an effort to rein in the group.

It also said Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada had warned the TTP leadership through backchannel communications to halt attacks against Pakistan or risk losing Taliban support.

The developments point to what appears to be a dual-track Taliban approach, continuing to provide the TTP space and support because of shared ideological ties while moving some fighters away from the border to reduce attacks on Pakistan, avoid a major escalation with Islamabad and address growing international concerns.

For Pakistan, however, relocating fighters deeper inside Afghanistan would do little to address the underlying problem as long as the TTP’s command, training and logistical networks remain intact.

Meanwhile, the TTP has continued to expand its organisational structure and operational reach.

The report said that following its annual rahbari shura in December, the group announced a revised structure with two new divisions covering Balochistan and the central region, and Kashmir and Gilgit.

The restructuring also included a new division described by the group as the “TTP Air Force”, suggesting an effort to broaden its operational capabilities.

In March, the group announced in several languages its spring campaign, “Operation Khyber”, calling for increased attacks against Pakistani security forces and civilians.

One of its deadliest attacks during the reporting period came on Feb 16 in Bajaur, where a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device martyred 11 security personnel and a child and wounded others. The TTP claimed responsibility and was reportedly operating from Afghan­istan, the report said.

Blurred lines

The UN assessment also points to increasingly blurred lines between terrorist groups operating in and from Afghanistan.

Al Qaeda’s official media outlet, As-Sahab Media Foundation, issued a statement on April 28 supporting the Taliban and, for the first time, backing the TTP in its operations against Pakistan.

The report said that while Al Qaeda had previously provided ideological guidance, training and support to the TTP, the latest statement represented more direct backing.

“One member state reported that BLA terrorists were trained along with TTP by Al Qaeda trainers in Afghanistan,” it said.

The report also noted that Al Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) formed the backbone of Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan, which was reportedly involved in several attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

AQIS leadership was reported to remain in Kabul after being issued tazkiras, suggesting “close cooperation between the Taliban and AQIS”, according to the report.

The assessment thus points towards a wider militant ecosystem rather than an isolated TTP problem, with training, facilitation and logistical networks increasingly cutting across organisational boundaries.

ISIL-K remains another major component of the threat. The report described it as the greatest threat to the Taliban authorities and the region, despite serious setbacks suffered as a result of counterterrorism operations by Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban.

ISIL-K was reported to have moved its operational infrastructure towards northern Afghanistan while dispersing training networks across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border region, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and retaining a presence in the suburbs of Kabul.

The UN report said ISIL-K was in a rebuilding phase, having shifted from attempts to hold territory to conducting fewer but high-profile, mass-casualty attacks, demonstrating resilience and adaptability.

Member states reported that the group possessed modern tactical equipment, including drones, night-vision devices and thermal imagers, and had received training in urban combat and the use of drones.

One member state also reported that ISIL-K and the BLA shared facilitation networks for logistics.

The report said ISIL-K attacks had declined in Afghanistan but increased in Pakistan.

On Feb 6, a suicide bomber detonated explosives during Friday prayers at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque of the Shia community in Islamabad, killing 32 people and injuring more than 150. The attack was claimed by a group calling itself ISIL in Pakistan but was likely conducted by ISIL-K, the report said.

The group also claimed responsibility for the May 5 assassination of Pakistani cleric Sheikh Muhammad Idrees in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The findings suggest that the threat facing Pakistan from Afghanistan is becoming more complex, with the TTP retaining Taliban ideological and logistical support, Al Qaeda providing training and ideological backing and ISIL-K and the BLA benefiting from overlapping facilitation networks.

The Taliban’s reported relocation of TTP fighters and warning to its leadership may reduce immediate pressure along the border, but the UN assessment does not suggest that Kabul has taken the more consequential step of severing its relationship with the group.

Published in Dawn, August 13th, 2026

World.title: 'We aspire for it to grow': Turkiye's Erdogan eyes expansion of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, aimed at stabilising a region wracked by conflict.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed last week as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Iran war, which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily.

“Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Cairo has robust military cooperation with Ankara, but has given no indication it intends to sign up to the new security alliance, which contains a Nato-style clause saying any attack on one would be seen as an attack on all.

The five-month US-Iran war has upended the security architecture in the region and forced a rethink of decades of conventional wisdom rooted in US military supremacy.

Erdogan said the pact emerged out of the “new circumstances” in the Middle East with regional players seeking to assume greater responsibility for their own security and stability.

“Regional issues should be resolved by regional actors, and with this action, we consider that we have taken a first step toward achieving that goal,” he told the Saudi-owned newspaper.

“Resolving regional issues must be carried out away from formulas imposed from the outside. We know very well that solutions imported from abroad only bring disasters.”

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

On Monday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed that the defence pact was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

Israel ‘removing Palestine’ from world agenda

Erdogan also accused the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to “remove Palestine” from the world’s agenda.

“The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region,” Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart, Mahmoud Abbas.

“No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people’s hearts as they try to destroy it,” he stressed, vowing Turkiye would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

A strong advocate of the Palestinian cause, Erdogan has repeatedly lambasted Netanyahu’s government, accusing the Israeli prime minister of committing “genocide” in Gaza and of pursuing expansionist policies in the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond.

Abbas arrived in Ankara on Tuesday accompanied by his diplomatic adviser Majdi Khalidi, intelligence chief Majed Faraj and senior Palestinian official Ziad Abu Amr.

He met Erdogan on Wednesday with the pair discussing developments in the region in talks the Palestinian leader described as “important and fruitful”.

“I hope the decision to hold legislative and presidential elections in Palestine after a long time will bring good fortune … [and] will advance the reconciliation process,” Erdogan said, in a nod to the historic rivalry between Abbas’ Fatah movement and Gaza’s Hamas rulers.

Abbas also hailed the defence pact between Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad, saying it was “of utmost importance” and expressing hope it would help enhance security and stability in the region.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Re0.94, raises high-speed diesel by Re0.54
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.94 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.54 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs324.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.79 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 13 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Investigators seek NCCIA’s help to unlock Mir Raza’s digital footprint
World.content:
KARACHI: Investigators probing the murder case of young businessman Mir Raza Ali have sought the technical expertise of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to unlock the deceased’s digital footprint, it emerged on Wednesday.

IBA graduate and owner of the eatery Wafflix Mir Raza had gone missing on July 28 and his bullet-riddled body was found a day later in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

A seven-member team, headed by DIG Amir Farooqui, is currently investigating the case.

Sources said they are trying to retrieve Raza’s “digital records / WhatsApp account details” through the NCCIA to determine whether there is anything suspicious.

Police will not rest until killers are exposed, IGP tells Abad

They believe that unlocking his digital footprint could help untangle the case.

The sources said that the investigation team also recorded the statement of the online cab driver who dropped Mir Raza in Gulistan-i-Jauhar on July 28.

Abad expresses concern over Raza’s murder, extortion threats Also on Wednesday, the Association of Builders and Developers (Abad) hosted Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho at their office.

Abad chairman Muhammad Hasan Bakhshi said that the investigation into the Mir Raza case was undermining citizens’ confidence in state institutions. He said that his parents should be provided justice.

Bakhshi said that builders were receiving calls from numbers based in Uzbekistan and other countries and the extortionists were threatening to carry out bomb attacks on builders’ projects.

Speaking on the occasion, the IGP said that the police would not rest until the elements involved in the Raza murder case were exposed.

He said builders were among the groups most affected by extortion rackets and that the police would play their role in addressing their complaints and ensuring their protection.

He said action has been taken not only against those criminals whose names were provided by ABAD, but also against other extortionists.

The IGP further said that red notices had already been issued for extortionists operating from abroad. “The paperwork is lengthy, but the police have already done the necessary work in this regard,” he said.

He said that the crime rate in Karachi has declined by 14 per cent, while incidents of murder and violence across Sindh have decreased by 70pc.

Meanwhile, at a press conference, Ashraf Qureshi of Tehreek-i-Bahali Karachi demanded that a joint investigation team probe Raza’s murder.

Published in Dawn, August 13th, 2026

World.title: KP cabinet okays tax relief for Malakand, ex-Fata
World.content:
PESHAWAR: The Khy­ber Pakhtunkhwa cabinet on Wednesday approved two draft notifications granting sales tax relief to local service providers and industrial undertakings in Malakand division and the erstwhile tribal areas, and cleared a series of measures relating to education, youth employment, healthcare and compensation for victims of terrorist attacks.

One notification provides exemption from sales tax on services for local service providers, while the other exempts industrial undertakings established or operating in the erstwhile tribal areas and Malakand division from the obligation to withhold sales tax.

In an official statement issued after Wednesday’s cabinet meeting, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said the government had set a revenue target of Rs180 billion for the current fiscal year and expressed confidence that it would be achieved through sustained efforts to strengthen revenue mobilisation.

He appreciated cabinet members for interacting with people in their respective areas and urged them to continue such visits, stressing that ground realities could not be understood by sitting in offices.

He said interaction with the public would help resolve people’s problems and highlight shortcomings in service delivery.

“When you don’t allow corruption, stand by the truth and believe in merit and transparency, you will find a lot of people against you,” he said, alleging that nobody spoke about the reported Rs5.3 trillion corruption involving taxpayers’ money, while institutions turned against those who stood against the establishment.

Imran’s health

During the meeting, Mr Afridi also expressed concern over reports regarding the health of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan and accused the federal government and prison administration of failing to address the issue.

He said Imran had been “super fit” before being “kidnapped” and claimed that people did not trust assurances from representatives of the “fake” government that his health was satisfactory.

Mr Afridi said that when he was prime minister, Imran had allowed individuals with allegedly falsified platelet reports to travel abroad for treatment. He demanded that Imran be allowed to meet his personal physicians, family members, lawyers and friends, saying this was his constitutional right.

Education, welfare measures

Later, Information and Public Relations Minister Shafi Jan told the media that the cabinet had approved an increase in the allocation for the Ehsaas Naujawan Programme from Rs3bn to Rs5bn in view of sustained public demand and a growing number of applications.

He said the flagship programme was aimed at promoting youth entrepreneurship, self-employment, financial inclusion and sustainable livelihood opportunities across the province.

It approved Rs188.8 million as a one-time, non-recurring grant-in-aid for the current fiscal year for model schools in the merged districts.

A grant-in-aid of Rs60m was also approved for Langlands School and College, Chitral.

Mr Jan said the cabinet approved the signing of an inter-departmental memorandum of understanding aimed at reducing the number of out-of-school children in the province.

As part of education reforms, the cabinet approved a semester-wise “jacketed” textbook system for grades KG to V from the academic year 2027-28, with grades VI to VIII to follow later.

It also approved the provision of 100 per cent free textbooks to students of grades 9 to 12.

The jacketed textbook model, proposed by the KP Textbook Board, is aimed at reducing the weight of school bags and curricular burden by binding two or more core-subject textbooks under a single cover without altering the approved content.

The cabinet also approved financial assistance totalling Rs66.6m for the medical treatment of 21 deserving patients.

It approved the appointment of the chief executive officer of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Transmission and Grid System Company.

The cabinet approved enhanced compensation, in relaxation of the existing policy, for civilian victims of targeted militant attacks in Bajaur, providing Rs10m to the legal heirs of each deceased person and Rs2.5m to those suffering major or minor injuries.

It also approved a general increase in the standard compensation package for such cases, raising payments to legal heirs of deceased victims from Rs1m to Rs5m and compensation for those suffering major injuries to Rs1.5m.

Published in Dawn, August 13th, 2026

World.title: Saudi oil exports ‘go dark’ amid Houthi threat
World.content:
• Tankers in Red Sea switch off tracking to evade attacks; conflicting data clouds scale of export disruption

• Tehran says no major progress in talks with Washington

• Trump claims US has total control over Hormuz

DUBAI: Saudi crude exports from the Red Sea are increasingly vanishing from view as tankers switch off tracking signals to avoid attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, with analysts saying all recent Yanbu loadings have been conducted “dark”.

The Houthis declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia on July 20, targeting the US and allies in the Iran conflict. They’ve since claimed attacks on Saudi-linked tankers, Yanbu oil facilities, and Jazan refinery, leading vessels to turn off tracking signals.

The increase in “dark voyages” is complicating the assessment of Houthi threat impacts on Saudi crude flows. Ship-tracking firms have produced widely differing export estimates — data used by the International Energy Agency, OPEC and traders to forecast market trends.

In the week beginning Aug 3, data analytics firm Vortexa estimated Yanbu loadings fell to 2.38 million barrels per day from 2.71m the previous week. Kpler estimated a sharper drop to 1.78m bpd from 4.04m, while AXSMarine calculated a rise to 850,000 bpd from about 420,000 bpd.

Those trying to monitor shipments rely on a vessel reappearing on tracking systems once it has left the high-risk area, using satellite data to cross-check movements and fill in the gaps.

According to Vortexa’s George Morris and Kpler’s Nhway Khin Soe, recent Yanbu cargoes were loaded ‘dark’, meaning no AIS tracking was active, with about 70pc of Saudi west coast shipments lacking continuous AIS coverage since July 23.

Houthi attacks have reduced traffic through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, with vessel numbers down to 32 from 50. Saudi Arabia is rerouting more oil via the Suez Canal or Egypt’s SUMED pipeline, with Sidi Kerir loadings reaching a record 2.17m bpd, 90pc of which is Saudi crude.

Meanwhile, Iran and the United States remain at loggerheads over efforts to agree to a permanent end to the war in the Gulf.

There were no discussions to extend their ceasefire because, from Tehran’s perspective, the deal had no start date, a senior Iranian source said.

“One of the issues that is being discussed via mediators is the US returning to the interim agreement and defining a timeframe,” the source said. “There has been absolutely no progress on this issue.”

Both Iran and the US have stepped up rhetoric in the past two days. US President Donald Trump has claimed that the United States is in control of the Strait of Hormuz.

“The US has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I think we will keep it!” he wrote on Truth Social. “Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, a wall of steel, and there is nothing Iran can do about it.”

Meanwhile, Iran’s security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said the Strait of Hormuz would stay closed unless the US agreed to Iran’s conditions to end the war.

Published in Dawn, August 13th, 2026

World.title: 7 miners abducted from Balochistan's Chagai
World.content:
QUETTA: Seven miners working for a private copper mining company were abducted by a group of armed men in the Mahian Kaur area of Chagai district on Wednesday, officials said.

Company officials said eight armed men arrived in the area on motorcycles, entered the miners’ camp and took them hostage at gunpoint.

They remained in the area for seven hours. The mine is located about 18 kilometres west of Chagai town.

The attackers collected equipment, weapons from the guards and other items from the camp before taking away seven miners at gunpoint.

The abducted workers include four labourers from Gilgit — Wajahat, Wajid Shahid and Sabir — and three local workers identified as Ziauddin of Dalbandin, Shah Saleem of Mahian, Chagai, and Saeed Muhammad, also a resident of Mahian.

According to sources at the mine, the armed men also took away vehicles, including a Zamyad truck and a four-wheel-drive pickup, more than 20 solar panels, a motorcycle, bedding and kitchen equipment.

They also reportedly took 2,500 litres of diesel and 1,500 litres of petrol.

The sources said the attackers stayed at the site for several hours and carried out the operation without resistance before escaping with the abducted workers and equipment.

The incident was promptly reported to the relevant authorities. However, the seven workers and the equipment taken from the mine had not been recovered at the time of going to press.

The administration has launched efforts to trace the abducted workers and recover the stolen property, while further investigation into the incident is underway.

World.title: Water-starved citizens ‘squeezed’ further for more Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation revenue
World.content:
KARACHI: While the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) is widely blamed for failing to provide water in many areas connected to its piped network across the metropolis, the utility has burdened Karachi residents with higher costs as it notified a uniform 7.05 per cent increase in water and sewerage charges for its residential and bulk consumers.

The latest increase has marked the second major hike in just two years as in September 2024 the corporation had increased its monthly charges by roughly 23 per cent.

At the time, sewerage charges were set at nine per cent of water charges.

The decision draws widespread criticism from the public who have to rely on water tankers as the KWSC failed to ensure uninterrupted water supply in their areas.

Uniform 7.05pc increase in monthly water and sewerage charges notified

A notification published in the Sindh Government Gazette on August 10, 2026 made the increase official, following approval by the KWSC Board of Directors to revise both retail and bulk tariffs in line with the average Consumer Price Index.

Under the revised tariff, monthly water and sewerage charges for residential plots will be based on plot size, while fixed monthly rates have also been set for various categories of commercial establishments and shops.

The hike in water and sewerage charges triggered concern and anger among people, many terming it injustice to people who did not even get adequate water supply despite paying hefty bills.

Muhammad Irfan, a resident of Gulshan-i-Iqbal, said that they got water only twice a month and that too for hardly half an hour. “We still have to buy tankers and now we have to pay the full increased bill. Where is the justice in this?“ he asked.

A housewife from Model Colony, Sadia Butt, said that after electricity and gas, now the water had gone up too.

“With a seven per cent increase, everyone’s bill goes up,” she said adding that it was already so hard to manage expenses these days.

Abdul Ghafoor, a shopkeeper in Khokrapar, Malir, said that there had been no piped water in his area at all, still the water utility sent them a fixed bill without meters. “With this fresh hike, small traders like us will face more burden,” he added.

A resident of Saddar said: “The government says it will provide facilities. We don’t get facilities, instead the bill increases every year.”

KWSC officials said that the objective of the revision was to strengthen the corporation’s revenue base and generate sustainable resources for water supply and for the operation, maintenance and rehabilitation of the city’s sewerage network and other civic services.

According to KWSC data, the corporation collected Rs8.14 billion in the first four months of 2026, with average monthly revenue now exceeding Rs2.26 billion.

However, the KWSC’s recovery rate remains low as in FY24 only 36 per cent of billed grievances were resolved within the stipulated time under the previous system in financial year 2024-25.

The KWSC Act 2023 provides the legal cover for such revisions, empowering the utility to adjust tariffs annually in accordance with inflation without seeking fresh legislation each year.

The KWSC officials said that without additional revenue, service delivery would deteriorate further and the revision was also tied to the utility’s commitments under the World Bank-funded Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project.
